entry.title: A new point cloud network that can tell apart any two inputs without high-order features
entry.summary: A Complete Geometric Message-Passing Architecture for Point Clouds arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a new equivariant message-passing architecture for 3D point clouds and proves that it is complete, meaning it can distinguish any two inputs not related by the rigid motions and permutations it respects. Experiments show it separates challenging point clouds that distance-based message passing provably cannot distinguish. entry.title: TwinD: a deepfake detector that generalizes from face blending to fully synthesized faces
entry.summary: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Facial deepfake detectors are usually trained on blended fakes, which paste generated faces into real frames and leave blending traces. Newer generators synthesize whole faces without such traces, and prior detectors perform poorly on them. The paper proposes TwinD, trained on FaceForensics++ fakes plus two kinds of twins made from real frames, and reports a mean AUROC of 96.3%. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose TwinD, trained on reconstruction and blob twins without any generator, reporting 96.3% mean AUROC across 19 datasets, 8.9 points above the prior best.

entry.title: Backbone Matters: Benchmarking Encoder-Decoder Networks for Driving-Scene Segmentation on BDD100K
entry.summary: Backbone Matters: Benchmarking Encoder-Decoder Networks for Semantic Segmentation of Driving Scenes on BDD100K arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines how the choice of encoder (backbone) affects semantic segmentation for autonomous driving. The authors combine four decoders (U-Net, FPN, LinkNet, PSPNet) with 13 backbones from six families, training all 52 models on BDD100K under one protocol. The best model, FPN with EfficientNet-B4, reaches 62.6% mean IoU and 89.8% accuracy. The backbone's effect depends strongly on the decoder.

entry.title: Can AI agents redesign engineering parts using over a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations?
entry.summary: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper examines whether a general-purpose large language model can drive simulation-based redesign of engineering parts. GPT-6 Astra modified a magnesium stent described by about 1,650 CAD parameters within a budget of 15 simulations, reading the full results of each solve. It lowered the objective, a high percentile of strains in the stent's bends, by 32%, while the industrial shape optimiser Tosca improved the original design by a tenth and then stopped.

entry.title: Beyond Alignment: Whitening, Profile Synthesis and Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition
entry.summary: Beyond Alignment: Whitening Geometry, Profile Synthesis, and Heterogeneous Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines why WiFi action recognition performance collapses when models move to unseen environments. Ablation and falsification experiments indicate the failure stems from the encoder extrapolating to novel environments rather than from domain alignment, and several alignment methods degrade results. The authors propose Dec-H, combining closed-form source within-class whitening, profile-mixing augmentation, few-shot adaptation and heterogeneous ensembles, which reaches 0.560 under K10 and improves consistently across four environments.

entry.title: Bradley-Terry training can distort outcome probabilities of accurate language world models
entry.summary: Bradley-Terry Training Can Distort Outcome Probabilities of Initially Accurate Language World Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies training language world models from comparative judge feedback using a Bradley-Terry objective, and finds it may fail to learn true outcome probabilities and can distort accurate ones. In a simulated robot push experiment, the objective moved a large share of probability onto outcomes that no enumerated branch produces. The authors attribute the shift to the objective itself, and report that a likelihood that knows the judge's rule learns from the same comparisons without this shift.

entry.title: Efficient AI agents that audit glitches in 3D worlds
entry.summary: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies automatic auditing of interactive 3D worlds built by AI agents, checking for glitches such as floating objects and walkable walls. A swarm of small vision-language explorers navigates and triggers behaviors, and a frontier model reviews their records and reports. On WorldAuditBench, the auditor succeeds on 55.9% of 213 tasks, outperforming the strongest reported auditor at under a quarter of its cost.

entry.title: How feedback-free self-evolution changes agent skills: a systematic study
entry.summary: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies what happens when models repeatedly rewrite expert-written agent skill documents without any tasks, run results, or judgments. Every model tested performed worse on every benchmark with the rewritten skills, dropping an average of 15 points on SkillsBench after thirty rounds. The authors propose SkillDiff, which marks expert knowledge in place without feedback or changing the skill text, raising SkillsBench pass rates by 4.8 points on average. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show feedback-free self-evolution degrades expert skills and propose SkillDiff, reporting a 4.8-point average gain on SkillsBench.

entry.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
entry.summary: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines where the gains from reinforcement learning post-training of diffusion transformers come from. The authors add a fixed set of input-independent steering vectors to the block outputs of a frozen base model, with 65 times fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA on SD3.5-M. Fitted to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints without any reward, the vectors recover 90.0 to 96.3 percent of reward gains across six image models and 89.8 and 111.9 percent on two video models. Trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed weight-based RL on text rendering and human preference scores. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that fixed, input-independent steering vectors recover 90-96% of RL post-training reward gains across several image and video diffusion models.

entry.title: Realized vs. population reliability: anytime-valid self-consistency certification under correlated reasoning
entry.summary: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper studies a method for certifying language model self-consistency by repeatedly sampling answers and stopping once an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold. It argues that reasoning samples are positively correlated, so the usual independence assumption fails and the certified hypothesis changes from a realized null about a drawn belief to a population null about average model behavior. Experiments on GSM8K and AIME show that this distinction matters differently across tasks, and that a prompt-level procedure restores population validity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate realized and population nulls under correlation, show the single-unit e-process fails for population claims, and propose a prompt-level procedure tested on GSM8K and AIME.

entry.title: Represented but misread: how post-training changes reading out a model's internal representations
entry.summary: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper compares linear probes with language models' own answers across six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions, analyzed with signal detection theory. Post-training lowered the sensitivity of the answers on average and changed how models use stated base rates. In a study of negated statements, post-training repaired cases where base models failed to use truth information their internal states already contained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate representation from readout and report that post-training changes readout rather than representation, testing six open models, checkpoints, model stitching, training experiments,

entry.title: Auditing LLM Intersectional Bias: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects
entry.summary: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies intersectional bias in language models, where people with several marginalised identities are treated differently than their separate identities would predict. It shows that a common audit criterion flags subgroups that independent single attributes already satisfy, producing many false positives on synthetic data. The authors propose ADDIS, which scores subgroups by their residual distance from an additive model and tests them against a Freedman-Lane null. Applying it to 13 open models on a synthetic Indian persona dataset, they find most flagged bias can arise from single-attribute effects, while a small set of interactions remains. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose ADDIS, separating interaction from additive effects via ARD scoring and a Freedman-Lane null, and report results on synthetic data and 13 open language models.

entry.title: Statistical inference for neural network models with ill-conditioned random weights
entry.summary: Statistical Inference with Ill-Conditioned Random Weight Neural Network Sieves arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper studies random weight neural networks, where hidden-layer parameters are randomly generated and fixed, and only output coefficients are estimated. It shows that such random sieves cannot stay uniformly well-conditioned as their dimension grows, so the smallest eigenvalue of the population covariance matrix vanishes. The authors develop approximation, estimation, and inference theory that accounts for this ill-conditioning, and report numerical experiments on finite-sample behavior. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove random-feature covariance eigenvalues degrade with dimension and develop ridge-adjusted inference theory, validated by theory and numerical experiments.

entry.title: GateTrace: Where Crowd Crossings Are Missed Under Occlusion
entry.summary: GateTrace: Where Do Crowd Crossings Go Missing Under Occlusion? arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Pedestrian tracking is used to count people at event entrances and passageways, but totals do not show which crossings were missed. The paper introduces GateTrace, which derives reference crossings from annotations under fixed rules, matches system reports by person, direction, time and position, and traces where misses occur. On MOT20 development sequences, ByteTrack, OC-SORT and BoT-SORT recovered 38.9% to 46.7% of low-visibility reference crossings, compared with 98.1% to 99.0% at high visibility. ★★★★ Notable: The authors trace crowd-crossing misses by person, direction, time and position, comparing several trackers on MOT20 across two sequence groups.

entry.title: OffBeat: multi-camera 4D capture with staggered firing beyond frame rate limits
entry.summary: OffBeat: Multicoset Sampling for 4D Capture Beyond the Camera Frame Rate arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents OffBeat, which treats a staggered multi-camera rig as a spatially distributed multicoset sampler and derives camera groups and firing order from calibration alone. Because each timestamp is recorded by one group, short-lived primitives are less likely to flicker in novel views. In simulated staggered capture on N3DV, OffBeat outperforms the full 4DSloMo pipeline with video diffusion in mean dynamic-region PSNR. Between the first and last synchronized frames, it also outperforms the best synchronized method of each scene. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model staggered camera rigs as spatially distributed multicoset samplers and derive a lifetime condition for flicker-free primitives. The abstract reports 3.04 dB higher dynamic-region PSN

entry.title: SKILL.PNG: Learning AI Agent Skills as Optimized Images
entry.summary: SKILL.PNG: Learning Agent Skills in Pixel Space arXiv · Nov 20, 2026AI agents are usually specialized with text-based skills, which cannot be optimized continuously. This paper introduces Skill.png, which represents a skill as an image whose pixels are optimized by gradient descent through the vision encoder of a frozen vision-language model. In 9 of 16 settings across 4 models and 4 benchmarks, it outperforms text skills optimized with frontier LLMs, using 64 to 256 image tokens instead of roughly 900 to 2000 text tokens. ★★★★ Notable: The authors optimize skills as image pixels via gradient descent through a frozen VLM encoder, reporting gains over textual skills in 9 of 16 settings.

entry.title: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications
entry.summary: Sightline: Calibrated Data-Flow Summaries for LLM-Integrated Applications arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Sightline, a tool that determines which input placeholders actually affect a large language model's output in programs that call LLMs. It reads a recorded call in one forward pass, learns from labels which attention reads count as uses, and calibrates pruning so only a chosen small fraction of true flows are missed. On 2,103 unseen repository families and four models, it outperformed seven closest methods and a hidden-state probe. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove placeholders flow to outputs only via attention reads and calibrate pruning from reads, reporting 1.6 to 2.6 times more spurious flows pruned than the best of seven baselines across

entry.title: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
entry.summary: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents NariQ, a trellis-coded post-training quantization method that calibrates on tokens generated by the BF16 model in agent sessions rather than short web text. On Qwen3.8-27B, the 3.0 and 2.5 bits-per-weight versions match BF16 on DeepSWE, Terminal Bench, AIME, and RealWorldQA, while the 2.0 bits-per-weight version performs somewhat lower. The authors release the GGUF files and a llama.cpp fork for inference. ★★★★ Notable: The authors calibrate trellis quantization on BF16 agent-session tokens; they report parity with BF16 on DeepSWE and Terminal Bench at 2.5 and 3.0 bits.

entry.title: Less Than Meets the Eye: Action-Set Identifiability and Principled Abstention for 3D Physical Geometry
entry.summary: Less Than Meets the Eye: Action-Set Identifiability and Principled Abstention for 3D Physical Geometry arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies whether bounded camera motions can distinguish competing explanations of the same image, such as a corridor, its mirror reflection, or a picture on a display. Intervene3D selects camera motions by maximin separability and answers only when available motions separate the remaining hypotheses, otherwise abstaining. On a synthetic benchmark, abstention removed all confident answers on unresolvable scenes, and an adequacy test lowered wrong answers on curved mirror scenes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose maximin motion selection with abstention for 3D geometry ambiguity, reporting synthetic and real display experiments.

entry.title: The Delayed Societal Cost of Unfairness: How Decisions Reshape Populations So Fairer Policies Can Win Later
entry.summary: The Delayed Societal Cost of Unfairness arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies the societal costs of decision policies, covering both the decision-maker's loss and the unequal distribution of costs across demographic groups. It asks when a policy that is optimal on pre-deployment data can be beaten by a fairer policy once both are evaluated on the population each induces. Under Rawlsian and egalitarian fairness notions, the authors give conditions under which placing more weight on fairness lowers societal costs. They also find that when the decision-maker's loss is accuracy-based, post-deployment gains can come from declining qualification among decision subjects. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that post-deployment population dynamics can make fairer policies reduce costs for both stakeholders, deriving conditions under Rawlsian and egalitarian fairness.

entry.title: Testing whether AI chat assistants catch distress signals spread across a conversation
entry.summary: Evaluating safeguarding in multi-turn conversations with AI assistants arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Researchers worked with three community mental health support workers to build nine scenarios involving cues of depression, psychosis, or domestic abuse. They compared whether six widely used AI models gave the same safeguarding responses when cues appeared together in one message or spread across a conversation. Across more than 7,400 conversations, most models met the support workers' standards far less often when cues were dispersed. entry.title: Safe subgame resolving for multiplayer games
entry.summary: Safe Subgame Resolving in Multiplayer Games arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how to refine a precomputed poker strategy in real time in multiplayer games with hidden information, where safety guarantees were previously missing. The authors prove the first conditional safety theorem for uncorrelated multiplayer subgame resolving, giving a post-hoc certificate that bounds how much the best-response gap can grow over the blueprint. Experiments on three-player Leduc and up to six-player Kuhn poker show the certificate flags every harmful update. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first conditional safety theorem for uncorrelated multiplayer subgame resolving, bounding the best-response gap by four terms; experiments on Leduc and Kuhn poker.

entry.title: How deep a language model settles on a word, and how long people read it
entry.summary: The Depth of a Prediction: Where Language Models Resolve a Word Predicts Human Reading Time arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines the layer at which language models settle on a word's prediction, a factor that relates to human reading time. The authors read each layer's prediction with the tuned lens and summarize the change in surprisal across layers as a resolution depth. On eight English eye-tracking and self-paced reading corpora and ten GPT-2, OPT and Pythia models, words resolved later, and the words after them, were read more slowly. Resolution depth improves held-out prediction beyond final-layer surprisal, entropy and the best single layer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce resolution depth from layerwise tuned-lens surprisal and report it improves reading-time prediction over final-layer surprisal and entropy across eight corpora and ten models.

entry.title: When sounds turn heads: recovering event timing audio LLMs fail to state
entry.summary: When Sounds Turn Heads: Recovering Event Timing That Audio LLMs Fail to Say arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper finds that a few attention heads in audio LLMs track the queried sound, yet the model's final timestamps do not express what these heads track. The authors propose head-guided decoding, which needs no training, to rescore candidate timestamps using these heads while keeping the model's presence decision. The method improves timestamps for three audio LLMs across benchmarks, including recordings released after training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors find attention heads tracking queried sounds and use them for training-free timestamp rescoring, reporting mIoU gains on three audio LLMs and newer recordings.

entry.title: Gradient boosting with Kolmogorov-Arnold units for interpretable regression beyond pairwise effects
entry.summary: Gradient Boosting with Kolmogorov-Arnold Units for Interpretable Regression beyond Pairwise Interactions arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents MJBoost, a gradient boosting method for tabular regression that uses a Kolmogorov-Arnold unit as its weak learner. The fitted model decomposes exactly into main effects, pair effects, and a higher-order remainder, allowing interpretation beyond pairwise interactions. On synthetic data and the OpenML-CTR23 regression benchmark, it achieves lower test error than the explainable boosting machine (EBM), and it is competitive with EBM and LightGBM on classification tasks. ★★★★ Notable: Uses Kolmogorov-Arnold units as weak learners to go beyond pairwise interactions in interpretable boosting; the authors report gains over EBM on synthetic and OpenML benchmarks.

entry.title: Why Flat Drafts Stay Flat: Region-Mean Latents and Texture in Flow-Based Image Generation
entry.summary: Why Flat Drafts Stay Flat: Region-Mean Latents Govern Texture in Flow-Based Image Generation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies why flat color-block drafts can keep a flat look in pretrained flow-based image generators even under photorealistic prompts. It finds that flattening photo regions shifts their regional means in VAE latent space, and experiments on FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image show that adding the photo-derived regional mean field restores texture. The authors also propose training-free rendering methods and draft-conditioned LoRA adaptation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a cross-scale mechanism linking latent regional means to texture in flow generators, validated via controlled field-exchange experiments on FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image.

entry.title: Full-rank and stable sampling for tanh neural networks
entry.summary: Full Rank and Stable Sampling of tanh Networks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies recovering fixed-architecture feedforward tanh networks with P parameters from finitely many point evaluations. It characterizes the parameters where the realization map's differential has full rank and shows this set coincides with the regular parameters defined by Vlačić and Bölcskei (2021). The authors prove that almost every set of 2P+1 sampling points gives uniform-norm Lipschitz stability on compact subsets of this set, and that projected gradient descent and projected Gauss-Newton converge locally for exact observations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize full-rank parameters as regular ones, prove 2P+1 generic samples give Lipschitz stability, and show local convergence of projected gradient and Gauss-Newton methods.

entry.title: What anti-hallucination training actually achieves: saying less, cheap pruning, and the rest
entry.summary: What Does Anti-Hallucination Training Buy? Saying Less, Cheap Pruning, and the Rest arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines how much of the reduction in CHAIR scores from preference training for vision-language models comes from the model simply saying less, and how much a simple post-hoc probe can reproduce. It compares eight public methods on LLaVA-1.5-7B across several benchmarks, along with DPO checkpoints. It also measures how well DPO on the model's own samples labelled by the probe or a CLIP score recovers the gain of ground-truth-labelled DPO. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decompose hallucination reduction into saying less versus training gain, benchmarking against a frozen post-hoc probe across several models and benchmarks.

entry.title: How Reliable Are Language Model Explanations for Insider Threat Detection?
entry.summary: How Reliable Are Explanations of Language Models That Detect Insider Threats? arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper audits explanations from language-model detectors that flag insider threats in CERT's simulated workplace logs. It tests explanations by removing internal features and comparing the resulting score change against a similar control change. The authors introduce the tipping radius, which measures how sensitive the result is to the choice of distance metric. They report that explanations are fragile under this choice and that flag scores partly reflect who the worker is rather than what they did. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a tipping radius measuring explanation fragility to metric choice, auditing seven language models on CERT logs.

entry.title: Suppressing a hidden shortcut that limits gains from fine-tuning video language models
entry.summary: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies a shortcut in which Video Large Language Models learn to answer from textual patterns in their training data rather than from the video during supervised fine-tuning. The authors propose VETO, which projects the fine-tuning update onto the orthogonal complement of the subspace that text alone occupies in the base model's activations. Across seven VideoLLMs, VETO keeps the training-distribution gains of SFT, and on six benchmarks under distribution shift it outperforms SFT and relies more on the full input. ★★★★ Notable: The authors project SFT updates orthogonal to the text-only activation subspace, reporting gains across seven VideoLLMs and six shifted benchmarks.

entry.title: Measurable Does Not Imply Transportable: Checking Whether Model Explanations Hold in Future Field Trials
entry.summary: Measurable Does Not Imply Transportable: A Prospective Audit of Model Explanations in Multi-Year Field Trials arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines whether explanations of machine learning models learned from past data hold in genuinely future contexts. Using multi-year maize field trials, the authors evaluate 16 environmental concepts across forward-looking data splits. Coarse environment-level explanations transfer reliably, while genotype-conditioned yield explanations transfer poorly, and measurement reliability does not predict transportability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize prospective explanation transportability and report multi-year maize field trial results showing reliability does not predict explanation transport.

entry.title: Why Fewer Denoising Steps Can Inflate Physics Benchmark Scores
entry.summary: What One Sample Cannot See: Why Fewer Denoising Steps Can Score Higher on Physics Benchmarks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines how video generation models used as world models are scored on the Physics-IQ benchmark. It shows that Physics-IQ compares each generated video against a single real recording, so its scores can reward less variation among generated futures even when the predicted distribution becomes less accurate. The authors introduce Kernel Physics-IQ, which removes this incentive in expectation and requires only two independent samples per condition. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show Physics-IQ's single-sample scoring rewards reduced prediction variation, and propose Kernel Physics-IQ needing two samples, tested on five video models and controlled physical systems

entry.title: Do video models learn physics without a physics loss? Testing them with forced response
entry.summary: Physical Laws without Physics Loss? Probing Learned Dynamics in Video World Models through Forced Response arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper asks whether video world models learn physical laws or merely imitate motion. The authors study a suspended object whose support is shaken, adapting six image-to-video models to predict its motion using only a flow-matching loss. Using three tiers of tests based on Taylor expansions, they check whether the models reproduce linear response, resonance, and higher-order effects such as nonlinear softening. ★★★★ Notable: The authors test video models via nonlinear forced response and three Taylor-expansion tiers, reporting six backbones on pendulum and double-pendulum tasks and learned nonlinear softening rarely seen

entry.title: Differentially private score estimation and its use in score-based generative models
entry.summary: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how to estimate the score function of a data distribution while protecting individual training examples with differential privacy. It proposes a sampling-based private estimator using quadratic B-splines and the exponential mechanism, implemented via projected Langevin Monte Carlo, and derives an error upper bound along with a nearly matching private minimax lower bound. As an application, the authors build a differentially private diffusion model whose privacy guarantee does not depend on the number of denoising steps. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to support the theoretical results. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize private score estimation limits with a near-matching minimax lower bound and build a diffusion model whose privacy guarantee is independent of denoising steps.

entry.title: Keystone: Judging Early Previews to Guide Search in Diffusion Image Generation
entry.summary: Keystone: Judging Previews at Key Steps for Test-Time Search in Diffusion Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper argues that text-to-image diffusion models already reveal their final outcome in early denoising previews, but existing reward models judge these blurry previews poorly. It proposes Keystone, a training-free judge that converts a prompt into typed questions about objects, counts, colours and positions, answered by an off-the-shelf multimodal model. On GenEval with SD3.5-Medium, Keystone-guided adaptive search outperforms best-of-8 with other verifiers while using under half the generator compute. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a training-free judge of early denoising previews using typed questions, reporting gains over best-of-8 on GenEval with SD3.5-Medium at under half the compute.

entry.title: Sequential Probability Assignment Against Smoothed Adversaries with Unknown Base Measure
entry.summary: Sequential Probability Assignment against Smoothed Adversaries with Unknown Base Measure arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies sequential probability assignment, an online learning setting using log loss, where data is smooth and well-specified but the base measure is unknown. It proves regret upper bounds against both adaptive and oblivious smoothed adversaries, controlled by empirical ℓ∞ and ℓ2 Hellinger entropy respectively, using algorithms based on truncated empirical Hellinger covers. The authors also give a general lower bound showing the upper bounds are essentially tight for some natural classes, separating the difficulty from the case where the base measure is known. ★★★★ Notable: The authors study smoothed log-loss online learning with unknown base measure, giving regret upper bounds for adaptive and oblivious adversaries and a near-tight lower bound showing a separation from

entry.title: Posterior Matching Distillation: faster diffusion generation that keeps sample diversity
entry.summary: Posterior Matching Distillation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a method that compresses a pretrained diffusion teacher's iterative sampling into a few network evaluations. PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples to teacher posterior means at fixed noisy states, which recovers the teacher's full clean-image posterior at each trained noise level and supports any-step sampling within the trained timestep grid. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B report that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, with competitive or leading prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality scores.

entry.title: PlayCraft: Using AI Agent Play Experience to Design More Engaging Games
entry.summary: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces PlayCraft, a framework in which a vision-based AI agent plays a game and then uses its detailed play reports to revise the game for mastery. The system alternates between a playing stage, where a player agent learns over repeated episodes, and a crafting stage, where a crafter agent estimates player ability and adjusts the game toward a target learning progression. Evaluations across three intelligence settings show that PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes than initial games in most cases.

entry.title: TideCache: Faster LLM Serving with Smarter Cache Memory Management
entry.summary: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming arXiv · Nov 20, 2026TideCache is a serving system for hybrid large language models on CPU-GPU superchips that manages GPU memory across different cache types. It redistributes physical memory pages among caches behind fixed virtual addresses, and streams global-attention prefixes layer by layer into shared GPU slots to reduce GPU residency. A request scheduler chooses between resident and streamed execution based on request size and queue state. Evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven configurations against SGLang with HiCache, it completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns and reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20–59%.

entry.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Reusing Pretrained Video Transformers to Learn Actions Without Labels
entry.summary: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents O$^{2}$LaF, a method that learns transferable latent actions from unlabeled videos. It initializes both an inverse-dynamics encoder with learnable action queries and a causal, action-conditioned forward video generator from the same pretrained video DiT, optimizing them end-to-end through a compact bottleneck. The authors report state-of-the-art few-shot action probing and stronger zero-shot action transfer on navigation and robotic manipulation tasks. The framework also extends to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2 with competitive results.

entry.title: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation via Shared Prediction and Refinement
entry.summary: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation through Shared Prediction and Refinement arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents ScaleWorld, a causal video model that handles both low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within one shared backbone. It first predicts a low-resolution video chunk, then refines it to high resolution in a single step, without needing a separate refinement model. The authors introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD) to transfer skills from specialized teachers into a shared student. The paper reports that the approach achieves high-quality generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.

entry.title: AgentRoboCritic: Assessing Frontier Agents' Direct Robot Control
entry.summary: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper analyzes how frontier multimodal language agents control robots through low-level numerical actions across 12 manipulation benchmarks, action by action rather than only by episode success. It introduces AgentRoboCritic, a framework where the agent states a local intent for each action and a critic judges the outcome and failure mode against that intent. The analysis finds strengths such as recovery from local failures and zero-shot manipulation, alongside limits in grasping, alignment, and recovery across failure modes. The authors release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions and an open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%.

entry.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation: Generating Inertial Sensor Data in a Pretrained Encoder's Representation Space to Augment Activity Recognition
entry.summary: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper explores generating synthetic IMU data in the token representation space of Bio-PM, a pretrained biosignal encoder, to augment human activity recognition. Autoregressive transformer and diffusion decoders are trained class-conditionally on token embeddings rather than raw signals. On the WISDM benchmark across 51 subjects, combining synthetic-token augmentation with gravity-aware features raises leave-one-subject-out macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809.

entry.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp, Temporally Stable Metric Depth from One Camera
entry.summary: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents Depth Pro 2, a method for estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. The authors note that prior approaches trade off temporal consistency against boundary sharpness, and they train one scalable network that handles both images and video at native resolution. The authors report that the resulting depth maps outperform prior work on metric accuracy, sharpness, and temporal consistency together. Code and weights are publicly released.

entry.title: Choosing which features to measure by distilling an oracle teacher
entry.summary: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies Active Feature Acquisition (AFA), where a policy decides which features to acquire for each instance under a budget, since each measurement may carry a cost. The authors explicitly construct an oracle teacher at training time, using labels and unobserved feature values to rank candidates by their effect on the downstream predictor's error. This ranking is distilled into a deployable policy called OracleImitator via soft-target imitation. Across multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, it matches or outperforms existing AFA methods across budgets.

entry.title: PGX: a framework that helps humanoid robots carry out long multi-step tasks combining walking and manipulation
entry.summary: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework for humanoid robots performing long-horizon tasks that combine locomotion and manipulation. A predicate-based state machine manages task progression and recovery, vision-language-action models handle stage-specific manipulation skills, and world-coordinate locking maintains spatial consistency. The authors report experiments on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid, showing improved stage progression and task success rates.

entry.title: Coda-DaVinci: Rethinking Video Generation with Code2Video
entry.summary: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how agent-made 3D proxies can guide video generation, examining the effects of proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. It finds that coarse proxies favor natural motion while medium-grained proxies favor consistency. Based on these findings, the authors introduce Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive multi-agent framework that chooses between proxy-guided and direct generation, and report gains in instruction following, scene consistency, and physical plausibility.

entry.title: Testing whether vision-language models selectively access concepts, inspired by global workspace theory
entry.summary: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a tool that maps intermediate states of vision-language models to a shared semantic space to examine concept representations. It reports that multimodal concept information is readable and selectively accessed depending on the task, and that accessed concepts take part in downstream computation. The authors also find shared patterns of concept accessibility across model families and sizes, offering an experimental basis for studying global workspace theory in multimodal AI systems.

entry.title: Checking whether passing tests miss spec-violating chip bugs with an LLM
entry.summary: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents Verify the Verifier, a framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines traces from a passing UVM regression against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 were candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes, with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.

entry.title: ProtoDiffusion: Generating Multi-Layer Images with One Token per Layer
entry.summary: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images arXiv · Nov 20, 2026ProtoDiffusion is a latent diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. It generates layered RGBA designs from an image or text, with optional bounding boxes for layout guidance, and determines the number of layers itself. The paper reports reconstruction and generation results on the LayerD evaluation split and states that text-to-design runs 19.1 times faster than a same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.

entry.title: Grading Barrett's esophagus dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization, using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
entry.summary: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study used 969 H&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions to develop a deep learning system for grading Barrett's esophagus dysplasia. Patch-level classifiers first identified diagnostically relevant regions, then attribute-aware multiple instance learning classified each slide as non-dysplastic, low-grade, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set of 130 cases, the macro-averaged AUC was 0.96, with 98% sensitivity and 81% specificity for binary dysplasia detection. Performance was consistent across institutions without stain normalization.

entry.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Testing Bias in Multimodal Fast-Judgment Decision Models
entry.summary: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces MM-SystemOneBias, a benchmark that tests 13 multimodal decision models on 5,323 instances from nine public datasets and 11 task scenarios. It applies six paired interventions, including option order, option label, external judgment, image-text description, irrelevant information, and rating scale. The study compares seven decision-model and backbone pairs and reports that the decision models are generally more stable, and that accuracy alone misses changes in answer probabilities.

entry.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Spotting Deception in Language Models
entry.summary: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines whether label-free persona and knowledge directions in the middle layers of large language models can detect lies. The authors extend a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts, and compare the resulting directions against single-dataset probes and random directions. The persona direction outperforms some probes on three of four models but fails on Qwen, and on lies about knowledge it mainly tracks reply wording.

entry.title: AURA: Audio-driven streaming avatar video generation
entry.summary: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents AURA, a model that generates audio-driven talking-head video chunk by chunk using a rolling KV cache, needing only the current chunk's audio to begin. It targets low-latency streaming uses such as voice assistants and virtual avatars. Two sizes are offered, 1.3B and 5B, trained with a two-stage distillation pipeline that aligns the causal student with a teacher and then applies Distribution Matching Distillation. The authors release the weights of both models and a dataset of 30K synthetic videos with precomputed teacher trajectories.

entry.title: Cost-aware AI agent system that optimizes features for large fleets of ranking models
entry.summary: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents an end-to-end agentic system that selects features for many ranking models under shared and per-model resource limits. LLM agents propose hypotheses while deterministic tools run and verify experiments, combining feature rankings through blending and Pareto fronts before trimming to fit the cost budget. On production models, normalized entropy improved by 0.31% on average and pipeline cost fell by 2.3%, with a 0.20% gain in a primary online metric in A/B tests.

entry.title: A deterministic embedding method for extracting calcium imaging fluorescence traces
entry.summary: Deterministic Temporal Embedding for Calcium Imaging Trace Extraction arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a deterministic temporal embedding framework that maps pixel-wise fluorescence traces into a low-dimensional representation, where temporally coherent sources form spatially coherent regions. It optimizes a class-balanced cross-entropy objective using exact sparse attraction and a deterministic particle-mesh method instead of stochastic negative sampling. Experiments on synthetic and in vivo two-photon calcium imaging data show robust recovery of irregular, spatially touching sources.

entry.title: Window Lever: Longer Observation Windows Matter More Than Data, Capacity, or Architecture in Customer Forecasting
entry.summary: The Window Lever: Longer Observation Windows Outweigh the Observed Effects of Data, Capacity, and Architecture in Customer Behavior Forecasting arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies long-horizon customer behavior forecasting and finds that a longer observation window, the number of past weeks a model sees before its forecast week, improves accuracy more than adding data, model capacity, or newer architectures. Extending the window from 8 to 16 weeks raised log-space R² by about 0.070 to 0.107 at the 1M tier. The direction held across five public datasets, but the authors could not separate window length from calendar coverage, so they report a robust positive association rather than the size of a calendar-independent effect.

entry.title: Plan4D: A plannable generative 4D world model that predicts future video and geometry.
entry.summary: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Plan4D, a generative 4D world model that predicts future RGB videos together with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, point clouds, and scene flow. It takes an observed scene and text-specified actions as input. The model stitches Depth Anything 3 with LongCat-Video and adds an auxiliary DPT head for scene-flow prediction. The authors report state-of-the-art results in generative 4D modeling of environmental reactions on synthetic and real-world datasets.

entry.title: Simple private noisy SGD achieves minimax-optimal error under strong convexity
entry.summary: Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies whether the simplest differentially private version of stochastic gradient descent, Noisy SGD, can match the statistical optimality of standard SGD on strongly convex losses. Under Rényi differential privacy, the authors bound the parameter estimation error of a single pass with a fixed stepsize schedule and constant batch sizes. For strongly convex generalized linear models, these bounds match minimax lower bounds derived via the Score Attack framework, giving the first minimax-optimal rate for Noisy SGD in private logistic regression without poly-logarithmic terms.

entry.title: Hybrid Search for Maharashtra Government Schemes in English and Marathi
entry.summary: Hybrid Retrieval for Government Scheme Search in English and Marathi arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents a bilingual English-Marathi search system for Maharashtra government schemes and public services. It combines BM25 keyword retrieval with sentence-embedding similarity using equal-weight score fusion. On manually curated bilingual queries, hybrid retrieval with MahaSBERT raises mean reciprocal rank from 0.864 (BM25 alone) to 0.879 and precision from 0.781 to 0.808. The authors conclude that lexical and semantic signals are complementary, though gains over the strong BM25 baseline are modest and depend on the metric.

entry.title: Direct3D-V3: a diffusion transformer that generates 3D shapes directly in voxel space, with no latent compression
entry.summary: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents Direct3D-V3, a 3D generation framework that uses a diffusion transformer without a latent space, removing the variational autoencoder and modeling raw SDF voxel grids directly. An implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels suppresses non-watertight surfaces, and Marching Cubes converts predicted SDFs into meshes so rendered normal losses can supervise training. The model also predicts the conditioning image's camera parameters as an auxiliary task and can be extended to generative reconstruction with normal-guided refinement.

entry.title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training That Makes a Model a Better Teacher
entry.summary: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper proposes Skill-FT, which uses natural-language skills to steer a teacher model's rollouts toward desirable behaviors, then fine-tunes a target model on those trajectories. It also introduces AutoMaster, an autonomous system where an LLM agent designs these interventions through trajectory analysis, skill design, and data selection. Across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks with 4B and 9B target models, it improves mean performance over vanilla SFT by 1.42 to 8.99 percentage points. The authors also report that keeping skill instructions during SFT yields higher performance than removing them.

entry.title: GLiDE: A fast, calibrated decision model distilled from reasoning models
entry.summary: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents GLiDE, a family of decision models from 0.4B to 27B parameters that score candidate answers in a single forward pass without generating text or reasoning steps. It builds on Qwen hybrid language models by removing causal masking from full-attention layers, and transfers reasoning ability through soft-target distillation from multiple teachers plus progressive post-training on diverse decision tasks. The 27B model reports a hidden-set score of 71.52 with 92.9 ms median latency on one GPU, rising to 73.37 after checkpoint averaging and parameter-free recurrent depth.

entry.title: Grid cells as spectral successor features: a reusable basis for continual RL
entry.summary: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper builds a feature basis from the eigenvectors of a fixed reference policy's transition matrix, so successor features become scaled copies of base features with closed-form coefficients. Adapting to a new task reduces to linear regression on reward. In a two-goal gridworld, the agent keeps near-maximal return across goal changes, while SimpleSF and DQN lose most of their return at each change.

entry.title: SGAR: Fast Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Geometric Attention
entry.summary: SGAR: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction via Sparse Geometry-Guided Attention arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents SGAR, a feed-forward 3D reconstruction method that replaces dense global attention across all views with sparse attention. A lightweight learned key selection module chooses, for each patch, a small set of patches from other views that are likely to be close in 3D. SGAR can be applied to different feed-forward models through fine-tuning. The authors report that it runs up to 12 times faster than dense attention at 1,000 views, keeps stable pose accuracy where other sparse methods fail, and produces more complete geometry within the same time budget.

entry.title: Multimodal Error Detection in Chest X-ray Reports: A Language Model That Reads Image Evidence
entry.summary: Multimodal Error Detection in Chest X-ray Reports: A Large Language Model Reading Image Evidence arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents Rad-Linter, which checks chest X-ray reports against image-derived scores for nine pathologies to flag potential errors for review. A 1.5B-parameter language model fine-tuned with LoRA judges whether each report is consistent with the scores. On controlled counterfactual quads from OpenI, it reaches 98.5% pair accuracy versus 80.5% for a keyword-and-negation rule baseline, and 93.4% versus 75.3% on a second set of 181 quads.

entry.title: FLUID: A Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Framework for Situated Task Guidance
entry.summary: FLUID: Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces FLUID, a framework for modeling, evaluating, and enabling flexible interaction in multimodal task guidance. Using natural human-human guidance data from WTaG and HoloAssist, it links each intervention to its supporting evidence, necessity, and timing flexibility. The authors build a real-time guidance agent that achieves the best overall balance of response correctness, intervention precision, timeliness, and latency among evaluated systems, though speech overlap remains an area for improvement.

entry.title: SHUSH: A reward design that penalizes excess responses for proactive video assistants
entry.summary: SHUSH: Emission-Aware Reward Design for Proactive Video Assistants arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies when proactive video assistants should speak, not just what they say. It shows that MMDuet2's PAUC reward encourages timely replies but does not account for how many replies are given, which leads to over-emission. The authors propose an emission-aware F1 reward that uses exclusive span-emission matching to penalize false emissions and missed spans. On the visual subset of OmniPro, their policy replies 2.5x less often than MMDuet2 while improving timing F1 from 0.259 to 0.396.

entry.title: Predicting Future Build Results with BuildPredictor
entry.summary: Anticipating Future Build Results with BuildPredictor arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper explores using machine learning to predict continuous integration build outcomes, aiming to avoid wasted time and resources on unnecessary builds. The authors propose a random forest model using features such as changes to source and build code and code complexity. The model achieves median MCC scores of 0.82 within projects and 0.86 in a holistic setting, with historical build results being the most important features.

entry.title: A new algorithm for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
entry.summary: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima, both in theory and in practice. For a broad class of locally quadratic objectives, it establishes the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction. The method multiplies the classical Polyak stepsize by 4 and a mild damping factor, adapting to local curvature. Experiments show it reduces sharpness similarly to Sharpness-Aware Minimization, including in settings beyond the theory such as nonlinear teacher-student networks and fine-tuning of pretrained LLMs.

entry.title: Simulated pass search for football set pieces (a method that tests many possible corner and free-kick deliveries to find better ones).
entry.summary: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS), which treats corners and lofted free kicks as a distribution over possible executions and futures rather than one realised event. It simulates counterfactual deliveries and attacker set-ups in a world model and scores each future with a value model. Tested on 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches, the best available delivery was worth 0.0085 xG more than the one actually kicked (+28%).

entry.title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: A learned model that efficiently fuses partial observations and tracks uncertainty in nonlinear systems
entry.summary: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a latent space where their dynamics follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This allows closed-form data assimilation updates in latent space, while a Gaussian decoder maps the latent posterior to physical variables and is trained with a Gaussian negative log-likelihood. Experiments on benchmark nonlinear dynamical systems show accurate state estimation and forecasting with substantially lower online assimilation cost than conventional nonlinear methods.

entry.title: Bayesian optimization over a learned low-dimensional search space for drug dosing
entry.summary: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a Bayesian optimization method that uses an amortized inverse map of a simulator to restrict the search space, paired with a Gaussian process kernel aware of the original problem geometry. It exploits the low intrinsic dimensionality of the problem and derives approximation bias, information gain, and an intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret rate. The method is applied to personalizing drug dosing in Parkinson's disease, where numerical simulations show improved performance, including under simulator misspecification.

entry.title: Fixing the Last Mile: Region-Aware Guidance for Image Restoration Failures
entry.summary: Fixing the Last Mile: Failure-Aware Image Restoration with Region-Specific Guidance arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes Failure-Aware Image Restoration (FAIR), a method for correcting localized errors that remain after image restoration, such as artifacts on faces and text. Instead of applying one generative prior across the whole image, FAIR conditions a single-pass restoration model on where failures are likely and what corrective guidance each region needs. The authors report that this improves semantic accuracy and style consistency in critical regions while keeping other areas faithful, and that experiments show it resolves common failure cases and improves perceptual quality.

entry.title: A CPU inside an LLM: compiling exact computation into pretrained weights without gradient training
entry.summary: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper proposes a closed-form method that writes deterministic arithmetic circuits directly into the weights of pretrained language models, without gradient training or external tools. The authors apply it to IBM Granite 4.2 3B and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B and report accuracy on 6-digit arithmetic, outperforming a LoRA fine-tuning baseline. They also report memory usage and out-of-distribution trigger results.

entry.title: Mind2Act World: A benchmark testing robot reasoning, physical action, and how the two combine
entry.summary: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated robotic manipulation tasks drawn from five real-world application domains, each with three difficulty levels and two scene settings. Tasks are grouped into Mind (decisions based on past observations), Act (precise, timely execution), and Mind2Act (closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions). The evaluation finds that competence in one view does not transfer to Mind2Act, with the strongest agent succeeding in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The authors identify composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

entry.title: Should Belgians install an advanced energy management system in their electrified homes?
entry.summary: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ? arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This study simulates 500 representative Belgian dwellings in which fossil-fuel systems are replaced by controllable electric technologies, including heat pumps, electric boilers and electric vehicles, with photovoltaic systems assigned at current adoption rates. It compares model predictive control, the TreeC decision-tree method, a rule-based controller and an MPC with perfect forecasts. Average annual savings versus the rule-based controller range from 82.5 to 177.4 EUR, but these are modest compared with system purchase and subscription costs, which the authors say is not favourable to widespread adoption.

entry.title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift: Adaptive decisions on whether AI or a human expert should decide, as expert reliability changes over time
entry.summary: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies learning to defer (L2D), where difficult decisions are passed to a human expert, in settings where the expert's reliability fluctuates over time. The authors propose EDA-L2D, which uses a sequence model to condition the deferral decision on recent histories of expert outcomes. Experiments on image classification, medical diagnosis, and hate speech detection show it adapts better than prior L2D methods to diverse temporal patterns of expert reliability.

entry.title: Risk-controlled test-time adaptation for vision-language-action robot models
entry.summary: Risk-Controlled Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents R2-VLA, a framework that lets vision-language-action robot models adapt reliably at test time by retrieving expert demonstrations as context. A learned uncertainty predictor decides whether the model should act on its own or ask an expert for help. A task-level risk-control procedure calibrates the uncertainty threshold to meet a user-specified task failure risk requirement, and expert corrections are added to the retrieval memory over time. Experiments on three VLA backbones and four LIBERO benchmark suites show average task success improved by 9.2 to 11.2 percentage points.

entry.title: Asuka-FM: A system-architecture co-design for efficient text-to-image pretraining on a consumer GPU
entry.summary: Asuka-FM: A System-Architectural Co-Design Framework for Efficient Text-to-Image Pretraining on Consumer Hardware arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents Asuka-FM, a framework for pretraining a roughly 206M-parameter text-to-image Diffusion Transformer from scratch on a single consumer GPU (RTX 4090, 24GB). It combines an AdaLN-free dual-stream backbone, SPRINT sparsification that cuts attention FLOPs by over 50%, aspect-normalized RoPE with shifted square crop training for zero-shot virtual camera control, and a 10M-parameter Patch Detailer Head for pixel adaptation. The authors report about 160 GPU hours at under $55, with GenEval and DPG scores at 256px and 512px.

entry.title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Egocentric Dataset Capturing Human Intent in Manipulation
entry.summary: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset of 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes, built to record human intent behind actions. It has three tiers: an attention tier (10,000 hours) inferring gaze from headband camera video, an exertion tier (2,000 hours) recording surface EMG from armbands, and a cognition tier (500 hours) recording scalp EEG. The dataset also provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps, point clouds, head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations.

entry.title: AdaPixFlow: Learning Continuous-Time 3D Motion Across Scenes from Sparse Camera Views
entry.summary: AdaPixFlow: Learning Continuous-Time 3D Dynamics Across Scenes from Sparse Multi-view Observations arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Adaptive Pixel Flows (AdaPixFlow), a method that learns a continuous-time dynamics operator mapping multi-view RGB-D observations to 3D object motion. It fuses all camera views into a shared world-coordinate voxel grid and predicts a continuous velocity field without per-scene optimization or predefined motion models. On held-out PhysInOne scenes, it improves F1 over the strongest competing method by 2.5% for in-between prediction and 15% for future prediction. Applied zero-shot to Spring-Gaus, it improves future-prediction F1 by 12%.

entry.title: FFGaussType: One-Pass Conversion of Glyph and SVG Shapes into Compact Gaussian Assets
entry.summary: FFGaussType: Feed-Forward Conversion of Glyph and SVG Geometry into Compact Gaussian Assets arXiv · Nov 20, 2026FFGaussType converts extruded glyph and SVG icon outlines into Gaussian assets in a single forward pass, avoiding per-asset iterative optimization. A point encoder maps surface anchors to a feature plane, and a shared decoder predicts neural Gaussians carrying surface normals, separating geometry conversion from material and lighting choices. On unseen font families and test icons it reports 1.62 degrees normal error and 0.985 silhouette IoU, the best among compared feed-forward converters, with conversion taking 9.1 ms per asset.

entry.title: MemFolder: A Structure-Guided Memory Folding Method for Efficient Agent Memory
entry.summary: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Long-running agents accumulate large external memory stores, which raise storage, retrieval, and response costs. MemFolder uses cross-record structure to reduce memory in two stages: RecordFolder consolidates compatible records into fewer retrieval units, and ContextFolder encodes them into compact text, revising encodings when key facts are lost. It was tested on the text benchmarks LoCoMo, PersonaMem, and LongMemEval and the multimodal benchmarks M3-Bench-web and M3-Bench-robot. On Mem0, RecordFolder kept 99.0% of average performance across the text benchmarks with 50% fewer records.

entry.title: Exact Bayesian layers via characteristic functions: a sampling-free method for propagating uncertainty in neural networks
entry.summary: Exact Bayesian layers via characteristic functions arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces CF-Prop, an uncertainty propagation method that uses characteristic functions to compute the exact output distribution of a Bayesian ReLU layer without sampling, including in non-Gaussian settings. Building on it, the authors propose the variational inference algorithm CF-VI, which computes the evidence lower bound in closed form for likelihoods such as Gaussian, Poisson, and Gamma. On CIFAR-100, CF-VI achieves the lowest calibration error among tested methods, about 35% better than the next best. On a heavy-tailed insurance claim dataset, it captures tail uncertainty that other sampling-free and Monte Carlo methods underestimate.

entry.title: Seer: Helping Small Research Agents Plan Using Shared Prediction Models
entry.summary: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Seer, an inference-time framework that separates an agent's action proposals from learned models that predict tool responses and estimate action value. The two models are trained offline on real research trajectories and reused across different agents, and only the selected action is executed. Across several deep-research benchmarks, Seer substantially improves performance for different language models, such as raising GAIA accuracy for Qwen3.5-4B from 13.6% to 41.7%.

entry.title: Using LLM reasoning traces to build interpretable Q-matrices
entry.summary: Reasoning-Trace Analysis Using Large Language Models for Interpretable Q-Matrix Construction arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes Reasoning-Trace Analysis (RTA), in which a large language model generates attribute-labeled reasoning steps via chain-of-thought prompting, and these steps are analyzed to inspect each item-attribute assignment. Studies used simulated and empirical fraction subtraction items. Chain-of-thought-derived Q-matrices overlapped substantially with the reference matrix but less than directly generated ones, and varied more across replications. Trace inspection linked disagreements to item-type coding, labeling rules, and how operations were expressed as steps.

entry.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling humanoid robot intelligence using whole-body human motion data
entry.summary: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces Awaken-Human, a dataset of about 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video paired with synchronized whole-body human motion across more than 100 skills. It also presents Awaken-HI, a vision-language-action model that predicts both human motion and retargeted robot actions for humanoid loco-manipulation. The authors report that more human pretraining data lowers robot action prediction error and improves real-robot success rates. Awaken-HI reaches a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight tasks, outperforming GR00T N1.7 and π0.5.

entry.title: Efficient modelling of composite defects by coupling a spiking-memory world model to an FE solver
entry.summary: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents a Composites World Model combining a material encoder, a Spiking Neural Network memory block that tracks long-term material state, and transformer blocks that learn short-term strain. The model is trained in three stages and then coupled to a non-linear finite element solver to simulate composite structures containing embedded defects. Benchmarks against experiments on IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear, for pristine and wrinkled composites, report prediction errors between 0.4% and 4.8%.

entry.title: ZeroVLN: Navigation Learning Without Navigation Fine-Tuning of the Vision-Language Model
entry.summary: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain arXiv · Nov 20, 2026ZeroVLN is a slow-fast navigation framework in which a vision-language model issues movement decisions through a semantic tool-calling interface in natural language, and an action expert carries out continuous execution. The VLM brain receives no navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning, and both components are jointly improved through closed-loop reinforcement learning. On VLN-CE benchmarks it substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods, with only minor changes to the brain's weights and largely preserved general capabilities.

entry.title: Statistically controlled early stopping for cheaper language model answer selection
entry.summary: Sequential Anytime Valid Tests for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper proposes a stopping rule for inference-time alignment, where a language model samples multiple candidate answers per prompt and a reward model selects among them. Candidates are grouped by final answer and scored with reward-weighted self-consistency, and sampling stops once a dominant answer is certified, with error controlled by a tolerance α. The method, e-RWSC, uses betting supermartingales so the error bound holds uniformly over time. Experiments across several models, datasets, and reward models report higher accuracy than baselines at substantially lower token cost.

entry.title: Managing Home Energy Systems: Developing and Comparing Control Methods
entry.summary: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This thesis examines methods for managing batteries, heat pumps, and other home energy systems, comparing simple rule-based, optimization, and machine learning approaches through three simulations and one real-world experiment. It introduces TreeC, a machine learning method that learns energy management strategies that are understandable and perform competitively with approaches such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning. The real-world experiment found that TreeC and model predictive control performed worse on actual hardware than in simulation, due to insufficiently representative training data and unreliable real-time inputs. In electrified Belgian dwellings, the algorithms reduced costs, especially in poorly insulated homes and homes with EV chargers or photovoltaic installations, but on average the savings did not yet outweigh implementation costs and effort.

entry.title: WeMM-Video: Advancing Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
entry.summary: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This report presents WeMM-Video, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal models in 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B sizes that jointly process text, image, audio, and video. The models support both a fast direct-response mode and a step-by-step thinking mode, and were trained on about 1.2 trillion tokens. Evaluated on over 120 benchmarks, the flagship 35B-A3B model sets a new open-source state of the art on omni-modal video tasks, and the 9B model surpasses the larger Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct. The authors publicly release the models and their evaluation and reproduction pipeline.

entry.title: Training vision models so LLMs can edit their weights directly
entry.summary: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies whether training neural networks in a dedicated way helps large language models edit their weights directly. The authors benchmark five LLMs editing convolutional networks and vision transformers on relabeling and error-correction tasks across four datasets, with over 2,600 edits scored. They propose Edit-Ready Training (ERT), which rehearses closed-form weight edits, and report that it achieves the highest mean score among the evaluated baselines for two of the LLMs.

entry.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
entry.summary: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies flow matching, a generative modeling method that transforms a source distribution into a target data distribution. It addresses non-Gaussian source distributions and establishes a nonasymptotic convergence theory for Euler discretization sampling with linear interpolation. Under stated smoothness, variance, and second-moment assumptions, the sampler achieves total variation error at most a given tolerance within a bounded number of iterations.

entry.title: TacInno: Teaching vision-language-action models contact dynamics beyond vision and action
entry.summary: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces TacInno, which isolates tactile changes that cannot be explained by visual observations and executed actions, called tactile innovation, and uses it only as a training target. A tokenizer compresses future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy TacInno-VLA learns to predict this code, with no extra module needed at deployment. The method reports average success rates of 87.5% on six simulation tasks and 70.5% on four real-world tasks, exceeding the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points. Ablation studies examine visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction.

entry.title: Sharing Knowledge Across EU Water and Climate Projects with an AI Agent System
entry.summary: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents an agentic AI ecosystem that consolidates documents from three EU-funded projects (IMPETUS, NATALIE, and InnWater) into a domain-aware knowledge base. It uses a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline in which a ReAct-style controller allocates retrieval budget across domain collections and gathers evidence. Two embedding models fine-tuned for water and climate are used for retrieval. In a benchmark over the corpus, the approach improved Mean Reciprocal Rank by 26.7% relative to a single-domain embedding baseline.

entry.title: Comparing a simulation-pretrained autoencoder with PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
entry.summary: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how compactly the transmission matrices of multimode optical fibres can be represented, which matters because they are large and must be re-measured when the fibre moves. It compares a permutation-equivariant autoencoder pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured matrices with principal component analysis. At 62x compression, the autoencoder adapted with two measured matrices reconstructs a 50um fibre's matrix well enough to focus light at 98% of ideal enhancement. PCA is about ten times more accurate when fitted on all 163 real matrices, so the autoencoder's value is as a prior when few or no real matrices exist.

entry.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Generation Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
entry.summary: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper finds that leading video generation models often break physical and logical rules in multi-step reasoning and planning, which it attributes to training on solutions as fixed-length clips rather than chains of decisions. It introduces ViDecide, a framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, along with Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT) to fix failed decisions. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new multi-step robot planning benchmark, ViDecide reaches an average strict success rate of 83.8%, compared with 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method.

entry.title: SEEC: A Dataset and Benchmark for Self-Supervised External-Eye Representation Learning
