entry.summary: SEEC: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Self-Supervised External-Eye Representation Learning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces SEEC, a standardized dataset of 4.35 million external-eye images drawn from fourteen public face datasets, together with an evaluation benchmark. The benchmark covers embedding geometry, anatomical recovery and transfer, and disease classification for ptosis, thyroid eye disease, and craniofacial syndromes. The authors find that representation-level and functional-level results do not consistently align, and no single encoder is best on every task. External-eye-pretrained encoders outperform DINOv2 and MAE on cross-dataset anatomical transfer.

entry.title: Multi-regime causal discovery benchmark evaluating UCMT algorithms and ablation studies
entry.summary: Evidence from a Multi-Regime Causal Discovery Benchmark: UCMT Algorithms, Comparative Performance, and Controlled Ablation Studies arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This pre-registered internal study compares the UCMT causal discovery algorithm family with established methods across heterogeneous benchmark regimes. It also reports a separate controlled ablation of UCMT v2 Global components. UCMT v2 Global outperforms NOTEARS and DAGMA in some settings but trails leading permutation-search methods in others. Sparsity and BIC-based refinement materially affect some outcomes, while arbitration and automatic regime selection show no confirmed general improvement.

entry.title: EgoCaptioner: Detailed, Timed Captions for First-Person Videos
entry.summary: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026EgoCaptioner is a captioning method for egocentric (first-person) videos that combines a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's activity with timed step descriptions that mark key moments. The authors built 50,000 training examples using a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline and refined captions with Group Relative Policy Optimization guided by rewards for factual accuracy, temporal alignment, and avoiding fragmented narration. Across five egocentric benchmarks, the model reportedly performs best among evaluated open-source models and outperforms several proprietary baselines on certain tests.

entry.title: Faster self-supervised generative CT denoising using few-step sampling
entry.summary: Fast Self-Supervised Generative CT Denoising via Few-Step Sampling arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Low-dose and thin-slice CT images are noisy, which can hide fine anatomical detail, and clean reference images for supervised denoising are often unavailable. This paper proposes N2N-iMF, which learns to generate one noisy image conditioned on its paired counterpart and speeds up generation through few-step sampling. At inference, multiple independently sampled outputs are averaged to suppress noise. On simulated thin-slice brain and low-dose abdominal CT, and on real photon-counting CT brain scans, the method achieved lower error than DDIM sampling while reducing per-output generation time from 7.29 s to 0.43 s.

entry.title: Evaluating Drug-Target Screening Models Beyond Benchmark Scores
entry.summary: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper compares 13 released drug-target interaction models that recommend molecules for proteins and proteins for drugs across 711 FDA-approved drugs and 614 human proteins. Most pairs of models produced completely disjoint Top-10 lists, and some agreement reflected repeated preferences for the same candidates. Retraining the same architecture with different random seeds gave similar test performance but only about two overlapping candidates in top-10 lists, so the authors argue that benchmark performance alone does not show whether predictions can guide experiments.

entry.title: Contactless breathing rate estimation from thermal videos using a 3D neural network
entry.summary: Contactless Estimation of Respiratory Frequency Using 3D-CNN on Thermal Images arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents a deep learning method that estimates respiratory rate directly from thermal videos using a 3D convolutional neural network. It removes the need for complex preprocessing and manual region-of-interest tracking. To cope with small datasets, the model uses data augmentation and transfer learning from synthetic datasets. The approach reaches a validation R² of about 0.61 on both preprocessed and raw thermal videos.

entry.title: World models lean on learned priors over visual evidence
entry.summary: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how a world model can transfer physical rules across environments by using object motion and interactions in a short video to infer the current rule and predict motion from a new initial state. The authors introduce TailWorld, a benchmark that controls training imbalance and calibration informativeness and measures bias toward common dynamics. They also propose Rule Inference for Transfer (RIFT), which infers the rule from calibration interactions and applies it to prediction. Experiments on TailWorld report improved prediction accuracy and physical consistency under varying imbalances and distribution shifts, including better prediction of rare dynamics.

entry.title: HiSA: sparsifying the hidden dimension of attention in language models
entry.summary: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes Hidden Sparse Attention (HiSA), which keeps query and key projections but computes only a partial dot product, chosen by a static, parameter-free rule based on token positions. Unlike most sparse attention methods that sparsify over tokens, HiSA makes attention sparse along the hidden feature dimension. Models trained from scratch with HiSA performed better than with full dot products while computing about a third of the query-key products. The method also speeds up decoding and reduces memory use during inference.

entry.title: How Much Memory an LLM Agent Needs: Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory
entry.summary: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how LLM agents can learn from their own past runs. The method extracts short lessons from each episode, then merges them into a smaller set of guidelines that the agent receives at inference time. Experiments on the AppWorld benchmark show that the right amount of memory depends on the model: a strong model keeps improving with more guidelines, while a weaker model does better with a selected subset. The authors also describe problems encountered during deployment and distill recommendations for teams building agent memory.

entry.title: Learning from Context: Leave-One-Out Prediction in Jump Diffusions
entry.summary: Learning from Context: Leave-One-Out Prediction in Jump Diffusions arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies jump diffusion models, which generate discrete data through stochastic dynamics in an embedding space and also reset coordinates to embeddings of categorical values. The authors propose leave-one-out prediction, in which each coordinate is predicted from the corrupted states of the other coordinates. On Text8 and LM1B text generation and ZINC250k molecular graph generation, leave-one-out-based variants improve key generation metrics over matched unrestricted controls.

entry.title: Beam Model Technical Report: A Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model for Coding, Reasoning, and Agents
entry.summary: Beam Model Technical Report arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This report presents Beam, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters, built for coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks. It was pretrained on 23.8T tokens and reaches a 1M-token context window through a two-stage midtraining phase. Post-training used large-scale asynchronous reinforcement learning on 10.5K GB300 GPUs, generating over 100M rollouts. The authors report refusing or pivoting on 88.9% of harmful requests while complying with 81.5% of harmless ones.

entry.title: Linear-time neural process for interpolating irregularly sampled spatial fields
entry.summary: Mamba Flow Matching Neural Processes: Linear-Time Inference for Irregularly Observed Spatial Fields arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces MambaFlowNP, a neural process trained with conditional flow matching whose compute scales linearly with the number of points, for interpolating spatial fields such as daily maximum temperature from sparse, irregularly placed observations. A multi-directional Mamba-2 scan reads context and query tokens in one shared sequence, so each query is predicted from its own scan position. On synthetic Matérn Gaussian-process benchmarks it is competitive with the strongest attention-based joint-predictive baselines, and on NOAA temperature interpolation it achieves the lowest RMSE and CRPS with near-nominal coverage at every regional to continental tier, running 114 to 784 times faster. A single forward pass handles one million points in under a second on one NVIDIA L40S GPU.

entry.title: TRCF: A forecasting framework for irregularly sampled multivariate time series
entry.summary: TRCF: Temporal-Reference Complementary Forecasting for Irregular Multivariate Time Series arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes TRCF, a framework for forecasting irregular multivariate time series, such as those from healthcare and environmental monitoring. It pairs a compact channel-independent forecaster with a complementary channel-dependent branch that aligns observations at shared times and uses other variables to correct missing history. The two representations are fused and passed to a shallow multilayer perceptron for prediction. Experiments on four real-world datasets report the lowest mean squared error and mean absolute error in the main benchmark comparison, along with 17.28% to 87.98% lower peak inference memory than APN.

entry.title: Perfumer: LLM-Based Agent Framework to Speed Up Structure Relaxation and Band Prediction in First-Principles Calculations
entry.summary: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents Perfumer, a large language model-based agent framework that combines Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. On the tested structures, pre-relaxation with the Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement reportedly gave a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. The Perfumer-band model returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector and reports a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials.

entry.title: Context as a Resource: ClonAct, a Router-Free Architecture for Multi-Context Personal Agents
entry.summary: Context as a Resource arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper addresses how personal AI agents handle many concurrent tasks: a single shared session causes topics to interfere, while router-and-ticket designs lose information in handoffs and miss merge conflicts. It proposes ClonAct, which virtualizes context blocks without a router, using a pluggable context memory unit, in-place context cells, a synaptic bus with a trial merge gate, and a shared trunk. The authors report results across three multi-stream benchmarks and three model families, including raising true-conflict merge accuracy to 63.3% with 45.9% fewer prompt tokens, and 95.0% completion under continuous surge streams.

entry.title: DeepQuest: An AI framework turning Alzheimer's knowledge gaps into tested discoveries
entry.summary: DeepQuest: From Knowledge Gaps to Scientific Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces DeepQuest, an AI scientist framework for Alzheimer's disease research that is driven by knowledge gaps. It turns unresolved questions from domain reviews into testable hypotheses and ranks them by data feasibility and groupwise Elo ranking. On the OASIS-3 dataset it produced 42 feasible hypotheses and achieved a scientific finding rate of 95.24%. Findings cover neuropsychiatric symptoms and dementia risk, longitudinal amyloid spatial stability, and neocortical tau-associated clinical impairment, with some associations supported in the independent ADNI and AIBL cohorts.

entry.title: Teaching LLMs to follow reasoning instructions via minimal edits
entry.summary: Training LLMs to Follow Reasoning Instructions with Minimal Edits arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes edit-based training, a framework in which a model learns from its own reasoning traces through localized corrections. An editor finds the first point of failure in a sampled completion and proposes a minimal replacement span, and the model is trained only on these edited spans. Tested on Qwen3-32B with the ReasonIF benchmark, the method improves compliance with reasoning instructions compared with full-trajectory imitation and trajectory-level reinforcement learning, while largely preserving performance on untargeted tasks.

entry.title: Sirius-Tiamat: how far a one-pass decision encoder can be shrunk before its answers change
entry.summary: Sirius-Tiamat: How Small Can a One-Pass Decision Encoder Get Before Its Decisions Change? arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies Laya, a 421M-parameter encoder that scores answer options in a single forward pass, and asks how far it can be compressed before its decisions change. It counts decisions that differ from the full-precision model and measures calibration with expected calibration error on synthetic and out-of-family benchmark questions. The results show that different compression methods flip decisions at different rates, and that a single fitted temperature, needing no labels, restores much of the calibration.

entry.title: Alikbachan: a stratified benchmark for detecting hallucinations in Bengali LLM outputs
entry.summary: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper introduces Alikbachan, a Bengali hallucination-detection benchmark organized along cultural-distance bands, six task types, and a 32-mode hallucination taxonomy. It includes a 2,516-item test set and a 5,000-item gold-labeled set. Zero-shot LLM judges' performance varies widely across strata, and an open competition with 222 teams showed that Phase-1 rankings only weakly predict Phase-2 results.

entry.title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark Testing AI Reasoning Under Missing-Information Rules
entry.summary: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions arXiv · Nov 20, 2026ClosureBench is a benchmark that tests whether large language model agents follow stated rules for handling missing information, treating it as unknown or as false. Each base scenario is tested under three closure assumptions (OWA, CWA, LCWA) that differ only in how missing information is treated. Results across 960 instances show that overall accuracy can hide substantial closure errors, with some agents choosing unknown under LCWA even when told missing facts should be treated as false. The authors argue that AI agent evaluations should also check whether agents apply the correct assumption when information is absent.

entry.title: Online temporal rotations for 2-bit KV-cache compression in video diffusion transformers
entry.summary: Online Temporal Rotations for 2 Bit KV-Cache Quantization in Video Diffusion Transformers arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper addresses the memory bottleneck caused by reusing key-value caches across denoising steps in video diffusion transformers during long video generation. It proposes Temporal Rotation Quantization (TRQ), which rotates temporally adjacent cache frames before 2-bit quantization, using a tree of lightweight planar rotations and a shared Hadamard transform, fit online without gradients or weight changes. The authors report that at 2-bit precision, TRQ improves VBench subject consistency over the QVG method on LongCat-Video-13B and HY-WorldPlay-8B.

entry.title: OceanCoder: An AI Model That Builds Ocean Engineering Simulations, Checked for Engineering Accuracy
entry.summary: OceanCoder: A Verification-Guided Large Language Model for Automated Simulation Modelling in Ocean Engineering arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents OceanCoder, a large language model based on Qwen3-8B that automatically builds simulation models for ocean engineering. The authors created 12,000 verified training examples across 12 engineering task categories and used a three-layer verification framework to check inputs, completed analyses, and output plausibility. This verification also provides reward signals for GRPO training. Pass@1 rose from 0% for the base model to 46.77% after SFT and 51.43% after GRPO.

entry.title: Rigel-Ladon: a law for how a one-pass decision model's accuracy changes with the number of options
entry.summary: Rigel-Ladon: An Option-Count Law for a One-Pass Decision Encoder, Tested on Held-Out Option Counts and Held-Out Schemas arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper studies how the accuracy of Laya, a small neural network that picks among written options in one pass, falls as the number of options grows from 2 to 35. The authors fit a log-linear law on up to 6 options and test whether it predicts accuracy for larger option counts and held-out question types. The law predicted results for 7 to 12 options well but failed on a 35-label pool of five schemas.

entry.title: Selecting candidates from streaming data arranged in groups, while controlling false picks
entry.summary: Conformal Selection for Hierarchical Streaming Data arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies online selection of candidates that arrive one at a time from different groups, extending existing conformal selection methods beyond the standard i.i.d. assumption. The authors propose Online Hierarchical Selection (OHS), which builds rank-based e-values for between-group and within-group samples, and OHSF, a variant that uses response feedback to improve power. The methods are shown to control the false discovery rate under mild hierarchical exchangeability and data arrival assumptions, and experiments on simulated and real datasets demonstrate their effectiveness.

entry.title: Predicting how laser-printed metal parts warp, using graphs built from their 3D surface files
entry.summary: Predicting Surface Displacement Fields of Laser Powder Bed Fusion Parts Using STL-Derived Graphs and Part-Level Descriptors arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a two-branch graph attention network that predicts 3D surface displacement of laser powder bed fusion parts directly from graphs built on STL meshes. One branch learns geometric relationships between connected mesh vertices, while the other uses 12 part-level descriptors. Evaluated on 117 parts with part-wise five-fold cross-validation, the model reaches an R² of 0.946 and a mean absolute error of 0.0178 mm for displacement magnitude.

entry.title: FirstCross: Convex 3D reconstruction from sparse single-photon views
entry.summary: FirstCross: Convex Single-Photon 3D Reconstruction from Sparse Views arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces FirstCross, a network-free method for 3D reconstruction from single-photon lidar data. It solves a short sequence of convex problems on a voxel grid rather than relying on slow non-convex neural optimization. Compared with Transientangelo, it achieves lower depth error across all tested scenes, view counts, and flux levels. On real captures with 1% of the photons, it reconstructs an object in about a minute on one GPU.

entry.title: A control-theory approximation to how predictive coding networks learn
entry.summary: A Control-Theoretic Approximation to Predictive Coding Dynamics arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies two biologically plausible learning frameworks for neural networks, predictive coding (PC) and deep feedback control (DFC), and their relationship. The authors show that DFC is a local approximation to predictive coding dynamics near fixed points, and that the two are exactly equivalent in shallow linear networks. They also show that the deviations of this approximation can be reduced by relinearizing the feedback controller and approaching the output target through intermediate nudges.

entry.title: ResVision: Spectrum-matched resizing and context-preserving inspection for visual reasoning
entry.summary: ResVision: Spectrum-Matched Resizing and Context-Preserving Inspection for Visual Reasoning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026ResVision is a method that improves visual reasoning in vision-language models through two components. Spectrum-Matched Resizing chooses an adaptive global sampling scale based on image complexity, while Context-Preserving Inspection returns each inspected crop together with the complete working view. Evaluated on four frontier VLMs and 29 benchmarks, the full method performs best for every model, improving 3.36 to 4.94 points over the Direct Base.

entry.title: Language-oriented semantic modeling to extract a target language from mixed speech
entry.summary: Language-Oriented Semantic Modeling for Target Language Extraction arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper addresses Target Language Extraction, which isolates speech in a target language from multilingual mixtures. The authors propose a framework that adds language-specific semantic representations to acoustic extraction. A pre-trained speech semantic model is adapted using language-aware prompt conditioning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and its outputs are integrated into the extraction model. Experiments on the CommonVoiceMix dataset show consistent improvements over acoustic-only baselines, with up to 1.16 dB SI-SDR gain.

entry.title: C-LiTE: A lightweight AI model for learning features of individual cells in tissue pathology images
entry.summary: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces C-LiTE, a lightweight foundation model with 22 million parameters for learning representations of individual cells in H&E-stained histopathology images. It processes 64 x 64 pixel cell-centred crops at native resolution without upsampling, and was pre-trained on a dataset of 60 million TCGA cell-centred crops. Evaluated on seven public datasets, it achieves a mean macro-F1 of 0.670 under frozen-feature evaluation, approaching CytoFormer (0.682) with about 30 times fewer parameters.

entry.title: Actor-Predictor: A reinforcement learning method for meeting formal rule requirements
entry.summary: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes Actor-Predictor, a framework for reinforcement learning that enforces temporal safety constraints such as formal specifications. Instead of building an automaton, a predictor estimates whether a partial trajectory will satisfy the specification, and its learned features serve as auxiliary inputs to an actor optimized with GRPO and RWR. Experiments on grid world and Isaac Lab robotic tasks show it outperforms automaton-based baselines on LTL-constrained tasks and handles non-regular specifications such as a^n b^n.

entry.title: Client Exits: A Way to Make LLM Responses More Transparent to Users
entry.summary: Client Exits - A Way to Increase LLM Transparency on the Client Side arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Client Exits, a lightweight mechanism in which a large language model inserts predefined, machine-readable markers into its output, and the client decides how to present the added information as graphics, text, or speech. The authors built a prototype using a finetuned Qwen model and a modified LibreChat client, using three XML-based markers from the Question–Option–Criteria (QOC) approach. Across 100 test questions, the client-exit model included all three markers in every response, and an LLM judge preferred its answers in 66% of comparisons.

entry.title: Fast analysis of fault vulnerability in memory-based CNN chips
entry.summary: Scalable fault vulnerability analysis for ReRAM-based process-in-memory CNN accelerators arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a fast, scalable analytical framework to measure how vulnerable convolutional neural networks are to permanent faults on ReRAM-based in-memory processing accelerators. It scores vulnerability at the level of individual weights, kernels, and layers without exhaustive simulation. Comparisons with fault injection results confirm its effectiveness, with a reported speedup of roughly 10^4 to 10^5 times over exhaustive fault injection.

entry.title: BADAS-3.0: A Single-Camera Model for Real-Time Driving Perception and Planning
entry.summary: BADAS-3.0: Real-Time Driving Perception and Planning from One Camera arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents BADAS-3.0, a 1-billion-parameter video encoder with four small heads that uses about two seconds of footage from one forward camera. In under 50 ms it predicts current speed, the path just driven, a collision-risk score, and six candidate trajectories over 6.4 seconds. On five trajectory benchmarks it reports 44% lower minADE₆ than the 34-billion-parameter Alpamayo 2 Super, which uses six cameras. The authors also add two open-loop safety benchmarks, where BADAS-3.0 achieves a higher pass rate than every published planner tested.

entry.title: Who Moved My Z Boson? Finding Resonance Features Inside a Neural Network
entry.summary: Who Moved My Z Boson? Revealing Resonance Features Inside a Neural Network arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines ShellFlow, a generative collider physics model trained on real LHC data, to find internal features representing resonances such as the Z, J/ψ, and Υ. The network was never told which muons come from a resonance and was trained only to generate final-state particle kinematics. The authors use these features to change the Z boson mass between about 80 and 105 GeV, and show that removing the feature broadens the Z peak. The rest of the invariant mass spectrum stays mostly unchanged in both cases.

entry.title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
entry.summary: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper measures how much the problems raised by different reviewers of the same paper overlap in conference and journal peer reviews. Overlap at ICLR rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, with year-on-year increases at NeurIPS, ICML, and several journals. Using MELD, a detector of LLM-generated text, the authors find that reviews flagged as LLM-generated overlap more with each other than unflagged reviews do.

entry.title: What if chain-of-thought isn't enough? Retraining an LLM's inner reasoning with a structured decision method
entry.summary: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough? arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper asks whether a large language model's internal thinking style can be deliberately changed and whether doing so helps. The authors train models to follow Question–Option–Criteria (QOC), a structured process that breaks a task into explicit questions, competing options, and evaluation criteria, instead of relying on Chain-of-Thought. Across the reported experiments, QOC-based fine-tuning improves answer quality over non-fine-tuned base models, with particularly strong gains once models are large enough.

entry.title: dLoop: Looped diffusion language models with recurrent latent refinement
entry.summary: dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents dLoop, which restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a Prelude-Loop-Coda architecture and repeatedly applies a parameter-shared intermediate block to the same partially masked state. The extra loops add latent computation before tokens are committed, letting information across uncommitted positions integrate more fully and making predictions more reliable. Experiments on GSM8K, MATH, MBPP, and HumanEval show dLoop achieves the highest or tied-highest accuracy on every benchmark.

entry.title: Tracking Objects Through Assembly and Decomposition
entry.summary: Tracking Objects Through Assembly and Decomposition arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a prompt-free video task that recovers all object tracks and detects both decomposition and assembly events, without requiring an initial object prompt. The authors present Atlas, a zero-shot system that builds and jointly reasons over forward and reverse spatiotemporal partitions to recover object tracks and their transformations. They also introduce OmniST, a benchmark with dense annotations of both transformation types. On OmniST, Atlas recovers more than twice as many state changes as prior methods and remains competitive on existing decomposition-only benchmarks.

entry.title: A statistical method for checking whether AI language models were trained on specific data
entry.summary: A Statistical Framework for Training Data Auditing of Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes a statistical framework for determining whether particular documents or document collections were used to train large language models. It combines chunk-level membership evidence with Cauchy combination to score each document, then uses calibrated p-values for overall auditing and identifying suspicious documents. Case studies on BookTection, Pile-arXiv, Cosmopedia, and HealthCareMagic show the framework is effective and reliable for auditing pre-training and fine-tuning data.

entry.title: Digitizing analogue gauge readings automatically with computer vision
entry.summary: Digitization of Analogue Gauges using Computer Vision arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper develops an automated system that reads analogue pressure gauges using computer vision and deep learning, to reduce human error in manual monitoring. Three hybrid approaches are compared: OpenCV with Scikit-Image, OpenCV with ResNet18, and OpenCV with VGG19, using a dataset of 1,848 images covering a 0-10 BAR range. ResNet18 achieved 97.3% accuracy, well above VGG19 at 64.4% and Scikit-Image at 63.8%.

entry.title: Similarity-Based OSF Logic for Flexible SPARQL Query Answering
entry.summary: Similarity-based OSF Logic for Flexible SPARQL Query Answering arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents an updated version of fosf, a reasoner for fuzzy order-sorted feature (OSF) logic that supports flexible SPARQL query answering over RDF knowledge graphs. The latest release adds a similarity relation among sorts and a translation engine that compiles OSF terms into standard SPARQL. Queries undergo fuzzy ontology-aware rewriting before translation, returning approximate solutions so that queries inconsistent with the underlying ontology can still yield relevant results.

entry.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Bugs in Agent Skills
entry.summary: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper presents SkillBridge, a contract-based workflow with static analysis, dynamic validation, and repair stages, to find and fix agent skills that fail on different operating systems. It screens 3,270 skill-target-OS cases covering 1,090 skills across Linux, macOS, and Windows, then runs dynamic tasks and root-cause review on selected cases. Repairing the contract fields responsible for failures raises the reviewer-judged target-task pass rate from 30.6% to 38.4%.

entry.title: STAGE: A method that expands spatio-temporal graphs to discover cause-and-effect links across tweets with weak supervision
entry.summary: STAGE: Spatio-Temporal Augmented Graph Expansion for Weakly Supervised Cross-Tweet Event Causality Discovery arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of finding cause-and-effect relations across separate posts in disaster-related social media. It proposes STAGE, which starts from local causal seeds, retrieves related event occurrences, and uses a causal scorer to build weakly labeled cross-tweet pairs. These pairs train a multi-head Graph Attention Network over event representations and a spatio-temporal context graph. Experiments on California Wildfire and Hurricane Harvey show that cross-tweet supervision improves performance, and transfer between disasters is asymmetric.

entry.title: Prism: A Minimalist Design for Hierarchical Text Detection
entry.summary: Prism: Hierarchical Text Detection with Minimalist Design arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Prism, a minimalist framework for hierarchical text detection that localizes words, text lines, and paragraphs and recovers their structural relationships. It attaches parallel lightweight heads to a single-scale backbone feature map and rebuilds the hierarchy with an efficient geometric inclusion algorithm. The authors find pixel-level regression gives the best accuracy-efficiency trade-off among lightweight head designs. The paper reports state-of-the-art results on public benchmarks, including speed and accuracy gains over LRANet on CTW1500 and a PQ improvement over OmniParser V2 on HierText.

entry.title: The Stability Gap in Continual Reinforcement Learning: Temporary Drops in Past-Task Performance
entry.summary: The Stability Gap in Continual Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies continual reinforcement learning (CRL), where agents must adapt to changing tasks while keeping previously learned skills. The authors introduce a simple benchmark that varies observation representations while keeping environment dynamics and rewards fixed, enabling inexpensive and reproducible experiments. Using it, they show a stability gap: prior-task performance drops substantially after new tasks are introduced, then partially or fully recovers, even though the agent has full access to past tasks.

entry.title: Evidence-first ranking to resist cover and title manipulation in cold-start video recommendation
entry.summary: Beyond Covers and Titles: Evidence-First Ranking for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Short-video platforms rank new uploads using content features such as covers, titles and frames before any user has watched them. The paper introduces REAP, an attack using simulated platform re-encoding that raises a cold video's rank percentile by 32.0 points among unrelated audiences. It then proposes Evidence-First Ranking (EFR), which scores cold videos mainly from their body and admits packaging only through a bounded residual. On MicroLens-100K, EFR reduces the attack gain by 81% and raises cold-start Recall@100 from 0.1133 to 0.170.

entry.title: TwinLab-Bench: Testing AI Scientists on Self-Designed Experiments in Lab Twins
entry.summary: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs arXiv · Nov 20, 2026TwinLab-Bench is a benchmark for evaluating whether AI agents can design their own experiments, covering 52 tasks across physical sciences, life sciences, and engineering. Each task has a TwinLab agent that acts as the environment, executing the tested agent's experiments using records from real laboratories. Reports are scored against a hidden answer taken from those real laboratory records. The strongest frontier model averages only 45.0, showing these tasks remain hard.

entry.title: FastRoverVLA: Faster Vision-Language-Action Control for Off-Road Self-Driving
entry.summary: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving arXiv · Nov 20, 2026FastRoverVLA separates slow visual plan generation from fast motion-based execution for off-road autonomous driving. Between visual predictions, it reuses decoded plans and corrects a speed-curvature action buffer using the vehicle's measured motion. On ORAD-3D and RELLIS-3D, it reduces final displacement error over a 3 s horizon by 18.0% and 36.7%, while cutting Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by roughly 16.6 to 20.8 times.

entry.title: Predicting melt pool shape in metal 3D printing using physics-based features and pretrained models
entry.summary: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines how to predict melt pool width, depth, and melting mode in laser powder bed fusion, a metal additive manufacturing process. It replaces raw process parameters with two dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, that combine laser conditions with material properties. Seven models are compared across 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets. The dimensionless features perform comparably or better in most cases, reaching R^2 = 0.96 for cross-material depth prediction, and pretrained tabular foundation models generally outperform classical methods on classification.

entry.title: Attention drift regularization with adaptive initialization for robust visual recognition across domains
entry.summary: Attention Drift Regularization with Adaptive Initialization for Domain-Robust Visual Recognition arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper proposes DGA-CAFC, a framework for source-free domain adaptation that addresses attention drift toward spurious features and uniform source model initialization across all target domains. The CAFC module enforces feature consistency against counterfactual-inspired perturbations, while the DGASS module estimates domain gap severity via target prediction entropy and selects a matching source model variant. The authors report consistent improvements over recent baselines on SFDA and domain generalization benchmarks, and note CAFC can serve as a regularizer for domain generalization objectives.

entry.title: Learning causal structure in time series by finding local parents
entry.summary: Time Series Structure Learning with Local Causal Parent Discovery arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD), a constraint-based method for learning causal structure in multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity. It works locally-to-globally, sequentially finding the parent set of each variable to build the full graph. With an exact oracle, ITPD ran the fewest tests and used the smallest average conditioning sets compared with baselines. On graphs with 2000 nodes, it ran 2.3×, 9.1×, and 40.9× faster than iterative IAMB, DF-PC, and PCMCI, respectively.

entry.title: Attention Head Specialization: Sample-Complexity Phase Transitions
entry.summary: Attention Head Specialization: Phase Transitions in Sample Complexity arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how attention heads in multi-head attention specialize into distinct functions depending on the amount of training data rather than training time. The authors find that syntax-specialized heads in BERT emerge as dataset size grows. Using a solvable high-dimensional model, they show that specialization is a genuine phase transition in sample complexity, appearing as non-analyticity in test error and other observables.

entry.title: MixReact: physics-based humanoid robot control that reacts to text, audio, and video cues
entry.summary: MixReact: Physics-Based Reactive Humanoid Control from Multimodal Cues via a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents MixReact, a unified framework that lets humanoid agents react to text, audio, and video cues with physically executable behaviors in simulation. It combines a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers (DisCo-MoT) to predict the next state and a History-aware Action Transformer (HAT) to turn that state into closed-loop actions. Experiments across all three modalities report gains over baselines in fidelity, diversity, and physical consistency, and ablations show the components contribute complementarily.

entry.title: Frontier AI models can tell whether a single text was written by a human or AI, and even name the human author
entry.summary: Frontier models need only one text to unmask its human or AI author arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This arXiv paper tests whether frontier models, given just one text and a zero-shot prompt, can identify its author as human or AI, the AI lab if AI, or the specific person if human. The authors report that the latest models match the trained detector Pangram and explain their predictions in natural language. They conclude that people who have published substantial writing online face a bigger threat to anonymity than commonly assumed, and that defenses are limited.

entry.title: SpecWM: A Training-Free Framework That Turns Verification into Correction for Streaming Video World Models
entry.summary: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes SpecWM, a training-free inference framework for streaming video world models that verifies draft chunks using the target model's latent velocity field. The same verification step produces a reusable correction, and two thresholds decide whether each chunk is accepted, refined, or rejected. On the WBench Navigation benchmark, SpecWM improves visual quality at a 1.63x speedup over the target model and raises NavScore from 75.99 to 85.63.

entry.title: Learning a Fixed Activation Function and Reusing It in New Vision Networks
entry.summary: Learn, Freeze, and Transfer an Activation Function Across Architectures arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes a learn-freeze-transfer method: a five-parameter activation function, FAct, is optimized jointly with a source network, then frozen and reused in networks trained from scratch. FAct is a truncated Fourier series initialized from GELU. On ImageNet-1K, the frozen activation improves top-1 accuracy by 1.46 percentage points over GELU in a same-architecture ViT. It also achieves the highest mean accuracy in 15 of 16 settings across four smaller architectures and four image datasets.

entry.title: Learning to reason with images faithfully using adaptive training data selection
entry.summary: Learning to Think with Images Faithfully via Adaptive Data Selection arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies a problem in vision-language models that crop and zoom into image details: they often call the zoom tool without actually relying on the zoomed region. The authors attribute this to training data and propose adaptive data selection, which chooses questions where zoomed evidence can still help the model answer correctly, supported by a data synthesis pipeline and an adaptiveness reward. The method improves reasoning faithfulness and reports state-of-the-art results on visual search benchmarks, along with gains over compared baselines on multimodal hallucination benchmarks.

entry.title: A full/quad-polarimetric SAR version of the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition
entry.summary: A version of the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition for full/quad pol synthetic aperture radar data arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper extends the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition, originally designed for reflection-symmetric polarimetric SAR data, to full and quad polarisation data. Both versions are demonstrated on X-band F-SAR data over Vejers, Denmark. Differences appear mainly for very bright man-made targets, where the new version yields lower entropy and a clearer dominant scattering mechanism. Interpretation uses the Cloude/Pottier alpha-bar angle.

entry.title: Matching sample-only distributions with a density-free invertible transport method
entry.summary: Invertible Transport Between Sample-Only Distributions via Projected Characteristic Functions arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes Projected Characteristic-Function matching (PCF), a density-free method for learning an invertible map between a data distribution and a prior defined only by samples. It aligns the distributions using projected empirical characteristic functions, so it needs no density estimation, adversarial training, or paired observations. An optional transport regularizer is added to favor transformations with lower displacement while keeping endpoints aligned.

entry.title: Using reward mismatch between AI scores and expert judgment to find new materials
entry.summary: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines whether disagreement between a predefined reward and expert judgment in generative AI materials discovery can reveal materials the reward overlooks, using electronic flat bands as the example. The authors learn expert preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences agree with the numerical score on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere, favoring compounds such as KCo2As2 and CoGa that have partially flat bands.

entry.title: Neural networks that respect thermodynamics to model fluid states using Gibbs free energy
entry.summary: Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for a Universal Fluid Gibbs Free Energy Equation of State arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper uses Gibbs free energy as a starting point and introduces thermodynamically consistent neural networks to build a fluid equation of state, called GEoS. GEoS achieves average absolute relative deviations of 5.25% for vapor-phase and 3.96% for liquid-phase density test sets, outperforming conventional cubic equations and existing machine learning models. UMAP analysis shows most test molecules are extrapolation cases, indicating strong generalization. The PC-SAFT equation fitted using GEoS also maintains high predictive accuracy.

entry.title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Learning for Region-Specific Image Restoration
entry.summary: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents RegionAgent, an adaptive framework for restoring images where different regions suffer from mixed, non-uniform degradations. A vision-language model is trained with two stages of preference optimization: step-level DPO based on immediate restoration feedback, followed by trajectory-level DPO that accounts for how actions affect later restoration steps. The authors also build a regional restoration preference dataset with 10K action pairs and 20K trajectory pairs. Experiments on multiple datasets and ablation studies report strong restoration results under mixed and single degradations.

entry.title: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation
entry.summary: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents FlexVSR, a framework for streaming generative video super-resolution that works across continuous scaling factors while being supervised at only a few scales. Its core component is ReLSA, a lightweight latent adapter that builds and refines target-grid latents before they enter the diffusion transformer, so a frozen VSR prior can generalize to new scales. Experiments report reconstruction and temporal quality that are competitive or superior, lower latency than most native-scale streaming and offline baselines, and generalization to unseen scales.

entry.title: SpatialScout-V2: Can AI Agents Find Objects in Real 3D Homes by Exploring?
entry.summary: SpatialScout-V2: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore Real-World 3D Scenes and Localize Objects? arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces SpatialScout-V2, a benchmark that extends active mapping from simulated environments to real residential scenes. Built from 100 homes in Realsee3D, it covers 3,171 target objects across 29 categories, and agents must select recorded viewpoints and iteratively estimate object centers within a fixed interaction budget. Evaluating seven vision-language models, six achieved an all-target mean IoU below 20%, and the best model, Claude Opus 5.5, reached 22.52%.

entry.title: Budget internalization: fixed-budget RL trades test-time scaling for in-budget accuracy
entry.summary: Budget Internalization: Fixed-Budget RLVR Trades Test-Time Scaling for In-Budget Accuracy arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for reasoning models trained under a fixed rollout cap. The authors find that after training, models rarely use tokens beyond the training budget, gaining accuracy near that budget but failing to improve, and falling below the base model, at larger budgets. They call this effect budget internalization and observe it across several models and tasks. Ablations and supervised fine-tuning on truncated traces suggest it stems from length-censored post-training rather than an RL-specific objective.

entry.title: FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
entry.summary: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces the FrontierOR Challenge, which asks teams to build agentic workflows that design, test, and improve algorithms for many operations research optimization problems at once. Stage 1 releases 60 of the benchmark's 180 audited problems across six application categories and five formulation types, in weekly rounds of 15, while Stage 2 adds new problems with unseen instances. Two separately ranked tracks run either in a network-isolated sandbox with open-source dependencies only, or on teams' own machines with any software within a timed window. Each solution is checked for feasibility, and feasible solutions are scored by the ratio of their objective to a frozen known reference, averaged over hidden instances.

entry.title: StreamEgo: Real-Time Streaming Conversion of Third-Person Video to First-Person View
entry.summary: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents StreamEgo, a framework that converts third-person video into first-person viewpoints in real time, targeting AR/VR and robot demonstration synthesis. It combines a streaming dual-branch prior, a region-aware loss curriculum, and distillation into a chunk-wise autoregressive model. The authors report generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

entry.title: MultiBinder: Preventing Identity Mix-ups Among Multiple People in Personalized Video Generation
entry.summary: MultiBinder: Preventing Multi-Subject Identity Leakage in Personalized Video Generation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses identity leakage and blended attributes that occur in personalized video generation as the number of custom subjects grows. It proposes MultiBinder, a "bind-then-narrate" framework: an entity-aware Q-Former aligns each subject's reference image features with its entity phrase, and a multimodal large language model captures each subject's action from the prompt. These contextualized features are injected into a video diffusion model through dedicated conditioning pathways. Experiments on general and newly curated multi-subject benchmarks report significantly better multi-subject identity fidelity than existing methods.

entry.title: When Foundation Models Disagree: Calibrated Uncertainty for Slide Image Classification
entry.summary: When Foundation Models Disagree: Representational Heterogeneity for Calibrated Uncertainty in Whole-Slide Image Classification arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes CALIFUSE, a framework that fuses several pathology foundation models to estimate how confident predictions are for whole-slide image classification, rather than to maximize accuracy. It treats disagreement between encoder representations as a confidence signal, combining slide-level decision consensus with chunk-level evidence agreement measured by Jensen-Shannon divergence. Evaluated on seven WSI classification tasks, it improves calibration, misclassification detection, and selective prediction over the strongest single encoder and naive ensemble averaging while keeping competitive balanced accuracy.

entry.title: Public-private cooperation against cocaine trafficking at Rotterdam port, modelled with a simple agent-based simulation
entry.summary: Public-Private Cooperation in the Port of Rotterdam: An Agent-Based Toy Model of Cooperative Efforts Against Cocaine Trafficking arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper uses an agent-based toy model combined with a causal loop diagram to study how trust, cooperation, competition, pressure, enforcement and actor skills interact in public-private cooperation against cocaine trafficking at the Port of Rotterdam. The model is grounded in empirical data on that cooperation and tests responses to parameter shocks under different starting conditions. Over a simulated five years, isolated single measures yield limited gains, while combining trust-building, cooperation, moderate pressure and reduced enforcement friction raises effectiveness by 25% from baseline, versus 13% for increased cooperation alone. The authors present these findings as exploratory hypotheses that require further validation.

entry.title: A practical tool for collecting proprioceptive data from the Unitree GO1 robot
entry.summary: A Practical Proprioceptive Data Collection Utility for the Unitree GO1 arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents an open-source graphical utility that lets researchers record joint states, IMU, foot force sensor and gyroscope data from the Unitree GO1 quadruped robot without ROS expertise. The tool supports starting, stopping and labeling recordings in real time. The authors characterize 51 recordings made with it and train a terrain classifier on them, reaching about 38% accuracy across ten terrain classes (10% chance). They also note that a split ignoring recording boundaries inflates accuracy to about 99%.

entry.title: Can World Models Predict Rice Growth? Toward Agricultural World Models
entry.summary: Can World Models Predict Rice Growth? Toward Agricultural World Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper introduces agricultural world modeling, which predicts how a single plant photographed with its cultivar and camera view will look days to months later. The proposed AgroWM model first reasons about the plant's current and future growth stage and writes a Growth Script with numeric targets for height, plant area, and color, then edits the photo to follow it. On rice, it matches the target growth stage in 54.6% of forecasts, outperforming several baselines, and it also scores best on maize.

entry.title: Adaptive Observation: A Dynamic Evaluation Method for Post-Training Self-Improvement
entry.summary: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes adaptive observation (AdaObs), a mechanism for post-training recursive self-improvement that adjusts what is measured when progress stalls. A controller refines diagnostic detail, raises difficulty, and adds related tasks, while the fixed anchor benchmark remains the evaluation target. Across eight anchors in long-context reading comprehension and instruction following, AdaObs raised the mean score from 66.4 to 73.7 under a matched data budget, outperforming the anchor-only baseline.

entry.title: CryoGaussian: Explicit Gaussian Splatting for Heterogeneous Cryo-EM Structure Reconstruction
entry.summary: CryoGaussian: Heterogeneous Cryo-EM Reconstruction Made Explicit with Gaussian Splatting arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Cryo-electron microscopy determines molecular structures from noisy particle images, but rare compositional states and subtle continuous conformational changes are hard to resolve. The paper presents CryoGaussian, which fits an explicit Gaussian density representation to particle images with a differentiable rasterizer and learns particle-level and per-Gaussian latents to capture compositional and conformational variation. It reports state-of-the-art reconstruction accuracy on CryoBench and, on experimental data, resolves a rare 50S ribosomal subunit state and continuous motion in the pre-catalytic spliceosome. The rasterizer is also optimized for additive projection, cutting training time by 12.8 to 28.0 times.

entry.title: Better Retrieval Without Better Verb-Noun Binding in Egocentric Video Search
entry.summary: Better Retrieval, Not Better Binding: Pretraining Exposure in Egocentric Video Retrieval arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces Ego-ExBind, a diagnostic protocol for analyzing how pretraining exposure relates to verb-noun binding in egocentric video-text retrieval. It finds that zero-shot retrieval is positively associated with verb-noun pair exposure, while higher exposure is linked to larger noun-swap margins and slightly smaller verb-swap margins. The authors show that reweighting exposure input at inference can improve retrieval without improving verb-noun compositional understanding.

entry.title: Using learned reconstruction errors to detect AI-generated videos
entry.summary: Learning Reconstruction Errors as Spatiotemporal Evidence for AI-Generated Video Detection arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a detector for AI-generated videos that learns reconstruction errors as spatiotemporal evidence. It jointly optimizes a reconstructor and a downstream classifier so the errors are more informative, and it applies 3D convolution to consecutive reconstruction errors to capture temporal patterns without a separate raw-video stream. Experiments on over 30 existing AI video generators show competitive performance against baselines.

entry.title: Loss-Guided Tsetlin Machines: Making the Learning Objective Explicit
entry.summary: Loss-Guided Tsetlin Machines: Making the Learning Objective Explicit arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The Tsetlin Machine has no explicit loss function; its learning signal comes from a fixed margin-based update rule. This paper proposes Loss-Guided TM, which replaces that rule with a swappable explicit loss while keeping the Tsetlin Automaton and clause logic unchanged. It evaluates cross entropy, symmetric cross entropy, and asymmetric loss on six datasets covering multiclass, multilabel, and binary tasks. The method matches or improves accuracy and F1 on five datasets and substantially reduces calibration error with cross entropy.

entry.title: Deep learning that estimates tissue stiffness speed from MRI data
entry.summary: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents an end-to-end trainable method for magnetic resonance elastography that estimates shear wave speed (SWS) maps directly from undersampled k-space data. It combines a model-based neural network regularized reconstruction with a phase-gradient inversion (k-MDEV) step. On retrospectively highly undersampled brain MRE data, the method reduces NRMSE by 30% compared with total variation minimization, and it remains accurate at acceleration factors up to 19. The approach also generalizes to in vivo data.

entry.title: SenseAlign: Learning Predictive Representations for Drone-Based Active Urban Sensing
entry.summary: SenseAlign: Learning Decision-Aligned Predictive Representations for Active Urban Sensing with UAVs arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents SenseAlign, a reinforcement learning framework that coordinates a fleet of urban sensing drones to actively inspect a dynamic road network under partial observations. A privileged teacher agent first learns optimal sensing using future ground-truth traffic, and a student agent then learns to predict future traffic while matching the teacher's action distributions. Experiments on the real road network of central Barcelona, with 1570 road segments, show the method outperforms baselines across multiple utility formulations.

entry.title: Pareto-optimal, strategyproof data sharing between competing firms
entry.summary: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how firms competing in the same market can share data to improve their predictive models. It models each firm's profit through prediction precision and market share, and characterizes Pareto-optimal contracts. The authors propose a parametric family of data-sharing contracts under which all firms' relative market shares stay constant, and show that one contract in this family is both Pareto-optimal and strategyproof against under-declaring initial endowments. Experiments on a real-world dataset test the profit gains under this contract.

entry.title: HiUni: A unified multimodal model sharing one visual space for understanding and generation
entry.summary: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents HiUni, a unified multimodal model that uses the same pretrained vision-language model's ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both visual understanding and image generation, with task-specific computation limited to the output side. To handle difficult pixel-space optimization and the loss of fine spatial detail, it introduces a Pixel Diffusion Head and a lightweight HiGate pathway. Experiments report an average understanding score similar to the pretrained VLM, along with competitive results on image generation and editing.

entry.title: How network layout and uneven data across nodes shape decentralized learning, analyzed via spectral methods
entry.summary: How Network Topology and Data Heterogeneity Shape Decentralized Learning: A Spectral Analysis arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how network topology affects decentralized federated learning through information mixing and the relative contribution of individual nodes. It proposes a spectral framework in which the dominant eigenmode governs consensus trajectory and node influence, while non-dominant eigenmodes govern how disagreement propagates and decays. Under uniform neighborhood averaging, stationary influence is shown to be proportional to node degree plus one, and a bound relates model disagreement to spectral mixing and gradient heterogeneity. Experiments indicate nearly identical learning dynamics across topologies under IID data, while network size and connectivity affect how unevenly distributed information is learned under non-IID data.

entry.title: UniVEP: Joint velocity and endpoint prediction for robot manipulation
entry.summary: UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines which prediction target flow-matching robot policies should use when generating actions, comparing velocity, endpoint, and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction. It introduces UniVEP, which learns both targets jointly with consistency supervision and shifts from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise decreases, needing only one network run per step. Tests on simulated and real-world manipulation report higher success rates and lower inference latency with fewer runs than single-target baselines.

entry.title: Measuring how pathways interact inside networks by summing each path's full contribution
entry.summary: Revealing Pathway Interactions in Network Computations with Complete Path Contribution arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces Complete Path Contribution, a method that splits a network's output into the complete contributions of individual input-to-output causal pathways. It also presents an algorithm that finds the k strongest paths without checking every path, with runtime that empirically grows linearly in k. The authors apply the method to benchmark image classifiers and a mouse retina model, showing how excitatory and inhibitory pathway interactions shape network decisions and dynamic receptive fields.

entry.title: Training-free method for smooth multi-prompt long video generation
entry.summary: Frequency-Synchronized Boundary Coupling for Training-Free Multi-Prompt Long Video Generation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces FreqSync, a training-free framework for generating long videos whose text prompts change over time. It treats transitions between prompts as frequency-selective boundary coupling, combining Frequency-Synchronized Source-Conditioned Attention with Residual-Clipped Spectral Stitching. Adjacent segments share stable low- and mid-frequency structure and motion, while high-frequency prompt-specific details stay dominated by the target prompt. The authors report state-of-the-art transition smoothness and prompt alignment with strong perceptual video quality.

entry.title: Integrating LLM-based embeddings into production content recommendation retrieval
entry.summary: From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents LSER (LLM Session Embedding Retrieval), a content recommendation system for autodesk.com. It derives session- and history-level embeddings from a pretrained large language model and adds them as auxiliary user-side features in the retrieval-stage user tower, alongside existing sequence encoders. The authors build a nearline serving path that asynchronously refreshes user vectors, and an ablation study across the multi-content-type catalog validates the incremental value of the LLM features.

entry.title: Memory- and compute-efficient approximate gradients for online training of hybrid models
entry.summary: Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes gradient approximation methods that keep the full-trajectory adjoint recurrence while approximating only the pullback operators, computing exact pullbacks by automatic differentiation at sparse anchor states. Between anchors, sensitivities propagate either through the identity (Zero-order) or through a reused, frozen pullback (Pullback Reuse). The methods were evaluated on an incomplete Lorenz-63 model, a large-eddy closure for two-dimensional quasi-geostrophic turbulence, and bias correction in a multilayer quasi-geostrophic ocean model. Peak memory fell by up to an order of magnitude and runtime by up to fourfold, while approximate gradients supported hybrid-model training at comparable accuracy.

entry.title: RL only reinforces actions it sees succeed
entry.summary: RL Can Only Reinforce What It Sees Succeed arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how outcome-reward reinforcement learning changes a model's choices when pre-training knowledge conflicts with new observations, using a puzzle world where the prior and correct answer are exactly known. It finds RL can only reinforce actions it sees succeed, so when the right action is rare, learning succeeds or fails across runs. Whether a run takes off is predicted before training by the expected number of attempt groups in which the action wins, with about 35 groups giving even odds.

entry.title: Learning to predict how neural network layers' internal representations relate, from their computations
entry.summary: Learning to Compare Neural Representations from Parameterized Computation Graphs arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper asks whether similarity between internal representations of independently trained models can be predicted from their parameterized computations, without running them on reference inputs. It introduces a graph metanetwork that maps each internal site to an embedding from its upstream computations, accounting for hidden-coordinate permutation and attention-basis transformations. The learned predictors are reported to support layer retrieval and stitching candidate selection.

entry.title: Same Judgement, Different Scores: How Scoring Scales Shape LLM Judge Results
entry.summary: Same Judgement, Different Scores: Numerical Scoring Topology in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces numerical scoring topology, which describes a scoring scheme's structure in terms of scale width, granularity, offset, symmetry, and boundary placement. It presents the first systematic study of how these design choices affect zero-shot LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation across multiple benchmarks and judge models. The authors find that shifted and narrow ranges often cause the largest score deviations, while stronger and larger judge models show higher discriminative validity and greater robustness to topology changes.

entry.title: Understanding MoE model decisions beyond gradients: a method for explaining how expert-selection changes affect answer scores
entry.summary: Understanding MoE Decisions Beyond Gradients arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models make decisions. The authors propose a predictor that uses the model's own expert outputs and selection rules to estimate extra effects caused when replacing one expert changes which experts later layers select, and adds these to a second-order prediction. On questions from three benchmarks, the method reduces error in predicting answer-score changes by 60% on Qwen3.6 and 47% on Gemma4 compared with a multistep baseline using gradients and second derivatives.

entry.title: Controlling the H1-2 Humanoid Robot with a Brain-Inspired Simulated Neural Network
entry.summary: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a spiking neural network inspired by biology to control the Unitree H1-2 humanoid robot's walking. Three training schemes are compared: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture, reward-modulated spike timing dependent plasticity and e-prop, and backpropagation through time as a non-biological baseline. All use distillation of a reinforcement learning expert policy with dataset aggregation. E-prop reached a 100% survival rate, matching backpropagation through time, while the fixed reservoir and reward-modulated STDP reached about 43.7% and 11%. The authors also demonstrate brief bipedal stepping on a full-size H1-2.

entry.title: AltRA-Test: A test for whether LLMs can replace human annotators without shared annotators
entry.summary: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes AltRA-Test, a statistical test for deciding whether a large language model can replace human annotators, without requiring all items to be labeled by the same annotators. It resamples items and swaps one human annotation per item for an LLM annotation, then checks whether inter-annotator agreement stays statistically non-inferior to an all-human panel. The authors evaluate 18 LLMs and 5 prompting techniques on 20 datasets spanning text, image, audio, and video. About 100 items often suffice, and LLMs pass in roughly half of the setups, mostly depending on the task.

entry.title: DfD-GS: Using Defocus Blur to Recover Metric-Scale Depth and Synthesize New Views from a Single Viewpoint
entry.summary: DfD-GS: Defocus Image Prior for Metric-Scale Single-View Depth Estimation and View Synthesis arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents DfD-GS, a feed-forward framework that predicts a metric-scale 3D Gaussian scene from one all-in-focus and one defocused image. It uses defocus blur as a physical depth cue to estimate metric disparity and align a monocular depth prior to metric scale. Experiments on synthetic-defocus datasets show better metric depth estimation and novel view synthesis than single-image baselines, with a more stable scale under field-of-view changes.

entry.title: SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents
entry.summary: SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces SheetAlign, a framework for automating spreadsheet manipulation with locally deployable open-weight language models. It separates the process into deciding where to operate, what to change, and how to implement the transformation, grounding code generation in workbook observations and available operations. Without training, the grounded task interface raises Qwen3-4B's average accuracy on SpreadsheetBench from 13.5% to 29.2%. With stage-isolated learning and execution consistency, SheetAlign reaches 32.8% average accuracy on SpreadsheetBench and 30.1% on Domain-Spreadsheet, outperforming comparable baselines.

entry.title: Domain-aware conformal prediction for reliable spacecraft pose estimation across synthetic-to-real image gaps
entry.summary: Domain-Aware Conformal Prediction for Trustworthy Spacecraft Pose Estimation under Sim-to-Real Shift arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how to indicate when spacecraft pose estimates can be trusted, using conformal prediction to produce uncertainty sets with a coverage guarantee. On the SPEED+ dataset, the authors find that calibration on synthetic images fails to maintain coverage on real images, and many failures go unnoticed because the predicted sets appear valid. They instead calibrate on synthetic images translated to the appearance of real images, which keeps pose labels valid without needing labelled real data. Experiments with two translation models restore coverage at miscoverage levels of 0.1 and above and reduce silent failures from up to 43.5% to at most 3.3% of test images.

entry.title: GenSPARQL: A Generative Extension of SPARQL for Incomplete Knowledge Graphs
entry.summary: GenSPARQL: A Generative Extension of SPARQL for Incomplete Knowledge Graphs arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents GenSPARQL, a generative extension of SPARQL 1.1 that adds an operator, GENOP, to bind values generated by a large language model to query variables during query evaluation. A similarity join maps the generated names to graph entities, and the LLM is called only for bindings selected by other graph patterns and filters. In an evaluation with three open-weight LLMs, embedding similarity mapped 83% of the entities named by the LLMs, with only one incorrect match.

entry.title: Iterative Scarcity-Guided Exploration for Generative Auto-bidding
entry.summary: Iterative Scarcity-Guided Exploration: Bootstrapping Generative Auto-bidding from Narrow Support arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies auto-bidding in online advertising auctions, where diffusion-based generative bidding methods stall at suboptimal performance during iterative training on narrow, low-quality cold-start data. The authors attribute this stagnation to a collapse in signal-to-noise ratio. They propose Iterative Scarcity-Guided Exploration (ISGE), which alternates between a Judger that assigns scarcity scores to trajectories and an Explorer that generates high-scarcity, high-return trajectories. Experiments on the industrial AuctionNet benchmark show ISGE surpasses the Full-Dataset baseline within three iterations starting from cold-start data.

entry.title: Complete-SVD: A Function-Norm Method for Low-Rank LLM Compression
entry.summary: Complete-SVD: A Functional Norm Approach to Low-Rank LLM Compression arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes Complete-SVD, a post-training low-rank compression method for large language models. It minimizes the L2 distance between the logits of the original and compressed models, weighting all logit changes equally. Using linearization and a Kronecker-factored approximation, the objective reduces to a weighted SVD with a closed-form solution. With WikiText-2 calibration, it achieves the lowest C4 and PTB perplexity and improves IFEval instruction-following accuracy over prior output-aware methods.

entry.title: One-to-Many: Diverse, bidirectional image translation using rectified flow
entry.summary: One-to-Many: Diverse and Bidirectional Image-to-Image Translation via Rectified Flow arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Many paired image translation tasks allow several valid target appearances, yet training gives only one target per source. This paper proposes O2MFlow, a rectified flow model conditioned on an appearance latent, which handles one-to-many generation and backward translation within one framework. Across three benchmarks, it shows dataset-dependent trade-offs between forward diversity and fidelity, the lowest backward LPIPS-Dist among evaluated methods, and the lowest backward FID on two benchmarks.

entry.title: SlotFlow-GB: A neural network method for estimating how many overlapping galactic binary stars are present and their properties
entry.summary: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper addresses the challenge of identifying galactic binary stars from gravitational-wave signals that the LISA space antenna will observe, where signals overlap strongly in frequency. It presents SlotFlow-GB, a neural framework that outputs, in one evaluation, a probability distribution over the number of sources and parameter densities for each binary, without fixing the number in advance. Tested on year-long LISA simulations with up to ten binaries in a 2 microhertz band, the inferred count differs from the true count by at most one in 94% of cases. The distributions can also be used to initialize later likelihood-based parameter estimation.

entry.title: When rankings beat signs for recovering gradient direction under even nuisance
entry.summary: When Do Rankings Beat Signs? Gradient Direction Recovery under Even Nuisance arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how to recover a gradient direction in d dimensions from a linear signal plus an unknown differentiable even nuisance, by ranking batches of antipodal query pairs. It compares three ways of using the feedback: within-pair signs only, reversed cross-pair couplings that cancel offsets, and full ranking inequalities. When the relative shell variation is small, the reverse-coupling method localizes the direction in one round with near-lower-bound evaluation cost.

entry.title: Reference-free humanoid skateboarding learned with termination-shaped reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Reference-Free Humanoid Skateboarding via Termination-Shaped Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning framework that lets humanoid robots such as the K1 learn to skateboard through model-free learning, without relying on demonstrations or prior data. The method pairs task rewards with terminations that block exploitative behaviours, such as losing the planted board foot, standing with both feet on the board, excessive twisting, separating from the board, and unstable board motion. As the prevalence of these constraints changes during training, learning implicitly progresses from stance control toward sustained robot-board locomotion.

entry.title: How the EU AI Act Appears on Hugging Face: A First Look
entry.summary: Studying AI Act Mentions: A first look at the impact of the European Union's AI regulation on Hugging Face arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines explicit references to the EU Artificial Intelligence Act on Hugging Face, a major platform for sharing AI models, datasets, and applications. The authors collected over five million records and manually labeled about 1,500 that explicitly mention the Act. They found such references remain rare; repository cards mostly claim compliance or assign responsibility, discussions report alleged violations, and commits mainly update compliance-supporting artifacts. The authors suggest platform support such as automated checks and documentation templates, along with clearer guidance on the Act's scope.

entry.title: PaveSplat: A Gaussian Splatting Method That Stays Solid at Higher Resolutions
