entry.summary: PaveSplat: Resolution-Robust Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting with Residually Corrected Surface-Aligned Covariances arXiv · Nov 19, 2026PaveSplat is a feed-forward Gaussian splatting method that adds a learned residual to an analytic surface-aligned covariance so that surfels keep covering the visible surface at different rendering resolutions. On RealEstate10K, it achieves the best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS among single-Gaussian-per-pixel methods at scales from 1x to 8x. On zero-shot DL3DV, it leads in PSNR within its group and ranks first or second on SSIM and LPIPS. A coverage-hole analysis shows fewer uncovered pixels than both baselines under high-resolution re-rendering.

entry.title: Streaming-AAA: Real-Time, High-Resolution AAA Game Video Generation
entry.summary: Streaming-AAA: Streaming AAA Game Video Generation at High Resolution, High Frame Rate, and Low Latency arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents Streaming-AAA, a system for controllable, long-running generation of AAA-quality game videos for interactive play. It generates 1080p video at 43 FPS with 198 ms end-to-end latency on NVIDIA A800 GPUs while sustaining long gameplay sessions. The approach combines a redesigned VAE for efficient high-resolution decoding, diffusion forcing pretraining with an extended temporal horizon, and post-training distillation with memory compression.

entry.title: Fixing the digital twin, not the detector: training roadside LiDAR detectors on simulated data
entry.summary: Fixing the Twin, Not the Detector: Sim-to-Real Roadside LiDAR Detection from Digital-Twin Data arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper describes a pipeline for roadside LiDAR object detection trained only on digital-twin data, using a CenterPoint model. Most of its gains come from aligning the twin with the real site, including coordinates, point density, box conventions, and added pedestrians, riders, and street clutter. The authors report that systematic sim-to-real corrections typically keep a quarter to three quarters of their validation gain on the test set, whereas choices fitted to a few validation objects do not transfer.

entry.title: SEOYUN: Exam Documents Designed to Make AI Glasses Refuse
entry.summary: SEOYUN: Refusal-Inducing Exam Documents for AI-Glasses Pipelines arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents SEOYUN, a framework for designing examination documents that cause vision-language models receiving camera-glasses captures to refuse to answer, aiming to reduce the usefulness of unauthorized photos. It contributes a threat model, analytical limits, and an evaluation protocol, and distinguishes refusal from leakage of correct answers. The authors state that this version reports no model-performance, physical validation, or human-subject results, so it is a research framework rather than a validated defense.

entry.title: Hidden Correlation Errors in Group-Level Shared-Latent Decisions
entry.summary: Serialization Tax in Shared-Latent Exchangeable Decisions arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper shows that accurate per-item probabilities can still lead to poor group-level decisions when items share an uncertain latent state, since independent marginalization removes dependence from the aggregate. The authors call this error the serialization tax and quantify its variance and total-variation gaps, threshold separation, and link to decision regret. They propose TaxScore, which routes large hidden blocks with unresolved uncertainty near a decision boundary to richer posterior models, and report utility gains on MovieLens 1M and 10M audits.

entry.title: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding
entry.summary: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents ForeSeek, a video agent built on multimodal large language models for understanding long videos. Instead of reactively retrieving clips based on local saliency, it forms expectations about unseen time regions, checks them through targeted observations, and refines its search, backtracking when expectations fail. Experiments on five long-video benchmarks report better efficiency-accuracy trade-offs, with competitive or superior accuracy while observing 2.5 to 4.4 times fewer frames than the strongest search-based agent.

entry.title: FrontierReplay: Exact prefix caching for hybrid language models without splitting prefill
entry.summary: FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Hybrid language models combine self-attention with recurrent layers, which limits prefix reuse to exact saved positions. The paper presents FrontierReplay, a caching system that creates exact checkpoints at predictable structural boundaries, such as turn ends and branch points, without interrupting the prefill forward pass. It logs recurrent-layer inputs and uses a state-only replay kernel to build the target state, paired with a frontier-aware retention policy. The authors report lower time to first token, higher goodput, and preserved task accuracy compared with existing exact caches and approximate replay methods.

entry.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Test for Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
entry.summary: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper tests whether a language model built around a shared workspace actually computes with the information broadcast to its modules, a question relevant to Global Workspace Theory of consciousness. It proposes a causal protocol that transplants a message from another input, so that ignoring, relaying, and recombining the message each predict a different answer. In AFGW, a language model whose modules communicate only through a learned workspace, the transplanted message yields the recombination prediction in 97% of cases.

entry.title: When Agents Play Differently: Finding Where Game-Testing Bots Diverge from Humans
entry.summary: When Agents Play Differently: Localizing Human--Agent Behavioral Divergence with Conditional Distributional Testing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a stratified framework that computes nonparametric discrepancy statistics within contextual cells and discovers subgroup rules showing where agent behavior departs from human play. The authors find that session-level metrics dominated by win/loss outcomes add little beyond mean comparisons, while process-level metrics such as move efficiency reveal real behavioral differences. Applied to a commercial match-3 game, the method shows a playtesting bot diverging substantially from humans in some game modes but not others. The implementation is released as open source.

entry.title: System-One RSI: a training method that builds fast “muscle memory” for interactive agents through guided practice
entry.summary: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes System-One Recursive Self-Improvement (System-One RSI), which pairs a fast decision model with a team of reasoning agents. The online inner loop is an Observe, Orient, Decide, Act (OODA) cycle that turns visual observations into timed actions without calling a reasoning model. The offline outer loop has the reasoning agents revise the prompt and decision tree, capture interaction records, and update model parameters. Experiments in Snake, Zenless Zone Zero, and Black Myth: Wukong show Snake's mean score rising from 1.30 to 7.35.

entry.title: Xing-Audio-NVVASR: Improving Speech Recognition That Also Captures Sounds Like Breaths and Laughs
entry.summary: Xing-Audio-NVVASR: Scaling and Refining Supervision for Joint Recognition of Speech and Non-Verbal Vocalizations arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents Xing-Audio-NVVASR, a single end-to-end model that transcribes speech and tags six classes of non-verbal vocalizations inline. The authors build their training corpus of about 800,000 utterances through progressive data mining and iterative annotation refinement, using cross-auditing between two models and breath detectors. On four human-annotated benchmarks, the 1.7B-parameter model ranks first among nine models in both composite score and six-class Macro-F1, with a mean composite score of 64.46.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for fast diffusion models using shadow posterior matching
entry.summary: Reinforcing Few-Step Diffusion Models via Shadow Posterior Matching arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Few-step diffusion models are efficient but are hard to improve with black-box rewards because they are samplers rather than score models and must stay anchored to an undistilled teacher. The paper proposes Shadow Posterior Matching (SPM), which renoises generated samples into shadow inputs and takes reward credit from their shadow posterior. A regression loss derived from a KL-regularized reward objective turns reward values into a reward direction while keeping outputs tied to the teacher. On 4-step generators, SPM reaches higher rewards with less reward hacking than prior few-step methods.

entry.title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool for Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
entry.summary: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper describes turning an AI surrogate model that predicts fiber orientation in glass-fiber-reinforced plastic parts into a practical engineering tool for crash simulation at Honda. The system combines injection-gate setting support, voxelization, surrogate inference, automatic mapping to crash CAE models, and report generation in one GUI. The complete preparation workflow takes about 0.1 hours, compared with about 25 hours for conventional flow analysis, and crash engineers can run it without molding specialists. Using the predicted orientation field reduced the absolute peak-force error from 19.0% to 11.4%.

entry.title: Policy-improvement replay for continual reinforcement learning of vision-language models
entry.summary: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies continual reinforcement learning for vision-language models, aiming to learn new abilities while keeping performance on earlier tasks. It uses the policy improvement principle to replay historical prompts under the current policy, and proposes Contrastive Likelihood Replay (CoLiR) to select which prompts to store in limited replay memory. Experiments on MRCL with three Qwen3-VL model sizes show that CoLiR achieves the highest mean final accuracy and mean task accuracy among compared methods, while staying competitive on new-task performance.

entry.title: Looking Beyond Salient Labels: Complementary Semantic Guidance for Multi-Label Learning
entry.summary: Seeing Beyond the Obvious: Complementary Semantic Guidance for Salient Single-Positive Multi-Label Learning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses salient single-positive multi-label learning, where each image is labeled with only its most visually prominent class. The proposed CoST framework adds Coverage Prototypes, built from semantically relevant candidate classes, to complement the existing Salient Prototypes. It also introduces a ranking-based strategy that selectively refines soft targets for classes receiving stronger semantic support. The authors report strong performance gains over existing baselines on multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for Autonomous Machines (AULA)
entry.summary: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA) arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper argues that autonomous AI agents are being deployed faster than the governance infrastructure needed to constrain them, and that maturing communication protocols do not make their activity legally legible. It names the resulting gap in liability and rights allocation the legal attribution gap. It proposes the Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), which registers AI systems and data assets as legal objects tied to identified legal persons, governs them through cryptographically tethered smart legal instruments, and evaluates them at runtime. Each instrument can include a legal context clause that gives effect to the law in force at the time of the act.

entry.title: Learning How Actions Change Outcomes: Action Effect Matching for World Models
entry.summary: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces AFFECT, an auxiliary training objective that helps world models learn how small changes in actions alter future visual observations. It injects temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on human teleoperation, then trains the model so its generated videos respond to this noise as recorded videos do. Across OGBench simulation and real-world DROID and ALOHA-2 setups, AFFECT makes world-model rollouts more faithful to real outcomes. On DROID, the Pearson correlation between policy success rates in the world model and on the real robot rises from 0.47 to 0.79.

entry.title: Multi-View Transformer and Geometry-Guided ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On
entry.summary: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents GS-VTON-MVT, a three-stage framework for virtual try-on on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) captures of a person, so the person appears wearing a new garment. It jointly edits training views with cross-view self-attention, conditions a diffusion editor on the garment image plus depth and surface normals, and sets attention blending weights by camera-pose proximity. The authors report improvements in FID, KID, LPIPS-based cross-view consistency, and user preference on the 3D-VTONBench benchmark over general-purpose 3D editors and prior 3D try-on methods.

entry.title: Energy estimates by open-weight language models at different stated food weights
entry.summary: Energy estimates of open-weight large language models across stated food weights: a dose-response evaluation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Researchers tested whether seven open-weight large language models scale their food energy estimates proportionally when the stated weight of the same food changes. Using 168 foods from the USDA Food and Nutrient Database for Dietary Studies, each assessed at nine weights, they found that all models compressed their estimates and did not scale proportionally. Having each model state an energy density and multiply it by weight in code substantially reduced the error.

entry.title: Efficient sheet music reading with fewer labeled examples via active learning
entry.summary: Sample-efficient end-to-end Optical Music Recognition through Active Learning arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper explores active learning to reduce the manual annotation needed for end-to-end Optical Music Recognition (OMR) in low-resource settings. The method selects informative samples for labeling. Uncertainty-based and diversity-based sampling strategies are evaluated on staff-level and full-page music corpora. Confidence-based sampling performs comparably to oracle selection based on true error, and each scenario benefits from a tailored strategy.

entry.title: Power Tracking for Large-Scale EV Charging Without Overloading Transformers
entry.summary: Power Setpoint Tracking for Large-Scale EV Charging: Transformer-Constrained Charging Policy Learning with Self-Tuning Constraint Prices arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper addresses power setpoint tracking, where an operator follows a purchased EV charging profile without overloading shared transformers or undercharging vehicles. It proposes TC-CPL, which extends soft actor-critic with proportional-integral Lagrange-multiplier updates, a residual on the incumbent dispatcher warm-started from its demonstrations, and a transformer-aware shared encoder. In simulations on a 600-port, 122-substation district, overload falls sharply, tracking error drops 27%, and satisfaction rises from 0.959 to 0.989, while on a single 42-kW transformer, overload also falls but absolute tracking error is 22% higher.

entry.title: MorphTwin: Enriching deformable material responses from videos for morphable, interactive physical twins
entry.summary: MorphTwin: Enriching Deformable Material Responses from Videos for Morphable and Interactive Physical Twins arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents MorphTwin, a method for reconstructing interactive physical twins from video that captures how objects deform. It enriches local deformation modes so volume and shape responses can be controlled independently, while keeping standard spring forces and explicit simulation. Offline calibration maps shared relative response changes to stiffness updates on each reconstructed graph. On synthetic scenes, MorphTwin reduces Poisson's ratio error by 75.8% and Young's modulus error by 22.1% compared to PhysTwin, and real-world experiments show up to 14.4% lower future tracking error.

entry.title: Web search in Latin America: language models surface less local and diverse news than search engines
entry.summary: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper compares how conventional search engines and LLM-based search handle news about Latin America. The authors built a dataset of 1,901 current events across nine countries and submitted queries in varied languages and user locations. Language models returned less diverse news sources than search engines and showed even lower shares of local news, suggesting LLM-based search may reinforce geographical hierarchies.

entry.title: GaussTrans: A Gaussian Framework for Light Passing Through Many Transparent Layers
entry.summary: GaussTrans: A Gaussian Interface Framework for Multi-Layer Refractive Transport arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how to model surfaces of multiple stacked transparent layers so that light passing through them is simulated accurately. It proposes GaussTrans, which has three parts: Gaussian-Field Hybrid Surfaces, Transport-Coupled Refinement, and Primitive-Guided Implicit Intersection. The authors report that on datasets such as RefRef, the method achieves significantly higher accuracy with relatively low storage requirements.

entry.title: Using 3D point dynamics as a proxy for robot world models
entry.summary: Point Dynamics as Proxy for Robotic World Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes separating dynamics prediction from visual rendering in robotic world models. The method lifts the first frame into 3D points, simulates their response to the robot's motion with a learned point dynamics model, and renders the results as pixel-aligned videos that any video model can read. In controlled experiments on the DROID dataset, it reduced object motion error by 8.6% and 6.2% without degrading image quality, and by 8.1% on a real bimanual robot.

entry.title: DTS: A training-free tile scoring method that speeds up long-context sparse attention in LLMs
entry.summary: DTS: Delta-Based Tile Scoring for Efficient Long-Context Sparse Attention arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes Delta-Based Tile Scoring (DTS), a training-free, content-adaptive method for scoring tiles in sparse block attention. DTS selects query and key anchors based on local vector changes and speeds up anchor selection with parallel delta packing. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, its average RULER and LongBench scores stay within 0.10 percentage points of full attention, and it achieves a 3.3× prefill speedup over a PyTorch full-attention baseline at 512K tokens.

entry.title: Hellinger Decision Trees for Density Ratio Estimation with Finite-Sample Guarantees
entry.summary: Hellinger Decision Trees for Density Ratio Estimation: Finite-Sample Guarantees arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes estimating the log density ratio directly by minimizing a balanced Hellinger risk over additive ensembles of axis-aligned decision trees, trained with Newton boosting. It establishes finite-sample guarantees and derives an explicit convergence rate for the estimator. Experiments on synthetic and public datasets are reported.

entry.title: AGSR: Aperture-Guided Super-Resolution for Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary: AGSR: Aperture-Guided Super-Resolution for Gaussian Splatting arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses the loss of fine scene detail in 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering, where the projected covariance of each Gaussian primitive attenuates high-frequency structure. It proposes AGSR, a lightweight inference-time framework that contracts projected covariances and progressively fuses multi-aperture renderings using uncertainty-guided aggregation and transmittance and depth cues. As a plug-in for pre-trained 3DGS models, AGSR outperforms lightweight image-space super-resolution baselines on the Mip-NeRF 360 benchmark while maintaining real-time performance with up to 139k parameters.

entry.title: Fast-JEPA: A Faster Latent World Model for Planning Action Sequences
entry.summary: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that predicts the outcomes of complete candidate action sequences directly, avoiding costly recursive rollouts. It reports a 96.50% average success rate across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, with planning 2.41 times faster than INTACT. The authors also introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for testing planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and response delays.

entry.title: ROAM-GRPO: Boosting Reasoning Diversity in GRPO Training
entry.summary: ROAM-GRPO: Enforcing Reasoning Diversity in GRPO via Routed Off-mode Approach Mining arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper notes that common post-training of LLMs with supervised fine-tuning and verifiable-reward reinforcement learning tends to collapse outputs into a low-diversity mode. The authors propose ROAM-GRPO, an extension of GRPO that detects well-solved problems and prompts the model to produce distinct solution strategies, which an LLM judge verifies before self-distilling them into the policy. Trained on a 1,000-problem subset of MATH level 5 with Qwen3.5-2b, the method reportedly raises peak pass@16 by 4.7% and increases correct-answer embedding cosine distance by about 1.5 to 2 times.

entry.title: SpatialMem: A Memory Framework for Quantitative Spatial Reasoning Agents
entry.summary: SpatialMem: Building Quantitative Spatial Reasoning Agents with Hierarchical Memory arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Vision language models handle qualitative spatial reasoning well but struggle with quantitative spatial reasoning. This paper proposes SpatialMem, a memory framework that lets a VLM agent accumulate tool-use experience and use it to orchestrate vision tools. The authors also introduce MetricBench, a benchmark covering indoor and outdoor scenes and three quantitative spatial reasoning tasks. The method reportedly achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks.

entry.title: A lightweight hybrid method to reconstruct milling force from internal machine signals
entry.summary: A Lightweight Hybrid Approach for Milling Force Reconstruction from Internal Machine Signals arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a hybrid approach that uses internal machine signals and machining metadata to enable force-based monitoring on existing machines without extra sensors. A supervised machine-learning model predicts the average milling force, which parameterizes a static force model that reconstructs force behavior over one spindle revolution. Evaluated on one milling machine with varied process parameters, tools, and two workpiece materials, it achieves R² values of about 0.96 to 0.99 for average-force prediction and reconstruction.

entry.title: LIFT: Latent flow matching that predicts probabilistic cell fates from single-cell snapshots
entry.summary: LIFT: Latent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Cell Fate Dynamics with Single Cell Snapshots arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents LIFT, a latent flow framework that generates probabilistic cell states from lineage-informed couplings. Variational inference encodes alternative outcomes in a latent space, and a conditional prior allows sampling from the initial state alone. A Mean Flow decoder predicts future cell states with one decoder evaluation per sample, making large-scale Monte Carlo prediction of cell fate practical. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that LIFT recovers both population distributions and cell fate probabilities.

entry.title: Many Solutions, One Answer: How Search Order Sets Language Models' Default Answers
entry.summary: Many Solutions, One Answer: Search Order Shapes the Default Solutions of Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The study tests four open-weight language models on constraint puzzles that have several correct answers. Repeated samples concentrate on one default solution, which different models often share, though models still produce rarer solutions when added clues uniquely identify them. Changing the order in which entities or values are searched shifts responses toward the solution that order favours, while randomising the presentation broadens the range of answers used.

entry.title: Linguistic Structure of Dependency-Conditioned Embeddings: How Word Vectors Are Organised by Syntactic Relations
entry.summary: The Linguistic Structure of Dependency-Conditioned Embeddings arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how word representations learned from syntactic dependency relations are arranged geometrically. Four models trained on WikiText-103, two count-based PPMI and two Skip-Gram with Negative Sampling, are compared at global and local scales. The authors find that global structure is strongly shaped by the part of speech of context words, while local similarities are partly preserved across relations. PPMI-based representations show greater cross-relation consistency than SGNS-based ones.

entry.title: Validation-driven deployment of LLM inference platforms for agent workloads
entry.summary: Validation-driven Deployment of LLM Inference Platforms for Agentic Workloads arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents an end-to-end evaluation pipeline for serving agentic large language models, covering testing, sizing, pre-production, and production stages. Experiments show that replaying captured agent session traces reproduces per-session token load more closely than live re-runs, and that live, replayed, and synthetic workloads exercise different serving code paths. In a case study deploying four large mixture-of-experts models on llm-d, target models reached about half the optimal concurrency and roughly 60% of throughput on captured workloads versus public traces. The authors open-source the tools and release a trace dataset.

entry.title: Multi-Camera Rigid Object Tracking: Following solid objects with one or more cameras
entry.summary: Multiple-Camera Tracking of Rigid Objects arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a method for tracking rigid objects using one or several cameras. It aligns a 3-D model of an object with image contours by minimizing the error between predicted model points and those contours, updating camera parameters at each frame. The authors analyze the Jacobian matrix involved, identifying the minimal number of matches needed and the singular configurations that cause rank deficiency. Experiments with a complex ship part and up to three cameras validate the method, which can also serve as a camera calibration procedure.

entry.title: From Cases to Criteria: Reusing Past Evaluation Knowledge to Generate Task-Specific Rubrics
entry.summary: From Cases to Criteria: Reusing Evaluation Knowledge for Task-Specific Rubric Generation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper introduces RubricDuo, which organizes past query-rubric pairs into a Rubric Knowledge Graph that links evaluation dimensions, concepts, criteria, and queries. For a new query, it drafts a rubric from relevant concepts and retrieved historical cases, then refines each criterion using concept-linked historical criteria and their source queries. Experiments on RubricBench and HealthBench report that RubricDuo achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated automatic methods, both in agreement with human-authored rubrics and in downstream LLM judging.

entry.title: Does the Split Change the Result? Frozen Satellite Features vs. Fine-Tuned CNNs for Tree Species Mapping
entry.summary: Does It Depend on the Split? Frozen Satellite Features vs. Fine-Tuned CNNs for Tree Species Mapping arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper compares a frozen DINOv3 model with a linear classifier against a fine-tuned ImageNet ResNet-50 for classifying 20 tree species in 0.2 m aerial images from TreeSatAI. Fine-tuning clearly wins on the official split, but the authors find that 28.8% of test patches overlap training or validation patches. Under a spatial split with 2 km squares and a 200 m buffer, the two methods perform similarly and the difference is inconclusive. The authors release the spatial split and their code.

entry.title: Verifiable Reasoning in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding
entry.summary: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This review examines how clinical large language models can produce confident hallucinations and invalid reasoning that static benchmarks fail to detect. It analyzes how errors spread and amplify in multi-agent systems, the limits of process reward models, and neuro-symbolic approaches that constrain neural outputs with formal logic and knowledge graphs. The authors argue that clinical AI safety depends substantially on system architecture and propose that certification should audit reasoning trajectories alongside accuracy.

entry.title: The Cost of Requiring Verifiable Programs and Its Benefits
entry.summary: The Price of an Explanation: What Demanding Verifiable Artifacts Costs, and What It Buys Back arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper measures the costs and benefits of requiring generative models to output executable verifiable programs, using the 120-task ARC-AGI-2 evaluation set. Demanding programs reduced solved tasks from 93 to 68, but because programs can be checked against training examples, protocols can stop early once a task is explained. A short evolutionary search over already-sampled programs outperforms plain sampling at the same model cost. The methodology is also applied to decoder synthesis for quantum error correction.

entry.title: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Denoising Schedules for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Inference Schedules for Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper argues that diffusion language models should not use one fixed denoising schedule for every task, since the cheapest acceptable schedule varies by task, model, and sampler. It proposes TCDA, a deployment rule that uses calibration data and bootstrap bounds to certify the cheapest candidate meeting utility and guardrail criteria, falling back to the full schedule otherwise. Tested across seven datasets and two model families, it certifies reductions in denoiser evaluations with a stated bound on deploying infeasible schedules.

entry.title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
entry.summary: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper reviews machine learning methods for forecasting solar photovoltaic power output and proposes a reproducible workflow combining automated model search with explainable AI. The workflow is tested on an open dataset from a 16.32 kWp plant in Porto, Portugal, forecasting one day ahead using a 4 km numerical weather prediction grid. The best models reach a normalised RMSE of 11.6% of installed capacity, about half the error of smart persistence. After conformal calibration, nominal 80% prediction intervals covered 81.7% of observations.

entry.title: Meta-RTL: Evolving Agent Harnesses for RTL Optimization
entry.summary: Meta-RTL: Evolving Agent Harnesses for RTL Optimization arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents Meta-RTL, a framework that uses EDA feedback to evolve RTL optimization harnesses from a minimal loop, keeping the optimization model, EDA flow, and per-design budgets fixed. Across 20 development designs, Meta-RTL* reduces aggregate WNS/TNS violations by 7.8% and 11.0% compared with Dr. RTL, with area reductions on 70% of designs. Without further evolution, it transfers to 10 unseen IC-RTL designs, cutting WNS/TNS violations by 20.5% and 14.0% and total synthesized area by 12.6%.

entry.title: EvoMem: Time-aware video memory agent with self-evolving retrieval skills
entry.summary: EvoMem: Self-Evolving Skills for Time-Aware Long Video Memory Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026EvoMem is a time-aware memory agent for answering questions about long videos. It builds a hierarchical memory indexed by time and uses retrieval skills that evolve over time to guide what evidence is fetched, how memory is accessed, and when to stop. Skill evolution is treated as reward-guided policy improvement, accepting effective skills and rejecting weak ones without updating model parameters. The authors report an average accuracy of 60.1% across four long-video question answering benchmarks, an average gain of 8.6 percentage points over prior best methods.

entry.title: Reproducible AI workflow for analyzing and forecasting ship movements from open AIS data
entry.summary: Trustworthy Geospatial AI Workflows: Reproducible Maritime Analytics and Forecasting on Open-Source AIS Data arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a reproducible geospatial AI workflow for maritime analytics, built on damast, an open-source data-processing and machine-learning library from Simula Research Laboratory. Using AIS ship observations from several public data providers, it demonstrates metadata-aware validation, reusable processing pipelines, vessel trajectory construction, and reproducible machine-learning experiments. The forecasting stage is model-agnostic and is implemented with a Transformer-based vessel-trajectory model. The authors also outline a future extension toward trustworthiness-aware geospatial AI, which is not yet implemented.

entry.title: Coherent belief and opinion spread creates more echo chambers: corrected version
entry.summary: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how echo chambers form in social networks, where groups share one opinion, mostly listen to each other, and grow more similar over time. The authors extend an existing opinion dynamics model with classical belief merge operations, keeping beliefs and opinions coherent under shared values. They introduce measures for identifying echo chambers in both beliefs and opinions and simulate propagation under varying initial conditions and tolerance. Results confirm earlier echo chamber findings and show belief echo chambers emerge, with more of them when opinions and beliefs stay connected, though fewer agents are involved.

entry.title: A study of the execution trajectories of the ID algorithm
entry.summary: On the trajectories of the ID algorithm arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The ID algorithm determines whether an interventional distribution can be computed from observational data and, when it can, returns a formula nesting products, ratios and summations of conditional probabilities. This paper follows the calls of the algorithm to analyze these formulas and reports two main results. The single outer summation is fixed by specific lines and the exit, while the inner summations and ratios are formed inside the tail. A ratio keeps a summation in its denominator only when a repeated tail is entangled, and an ancestry test in the original graph can decide beforehand whether this can be avoided.

entry.title: Efficient tuning of self-supervised vision models for radar activity recognition under distribution shift
entry.summary: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Self-supervised Vision Backbones Survives Distribution Shift in Radar Micro-Doppler HAR arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper compares full fine-tuning, frozen probing, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for recognizing human activities from radar micro-Doppler signatures. Methods were tested on in-distribution cross-validation and few-shot transfer across age, orientation, and datasets. Only PEFT avoided both the negative cross-dataset transfer of full fine-tuning and the under-adaptation of frozen features. The authors pair DINOv3 with PiSSA adaptation, and their Small variant matches the prior Base-size PEFT method in-distribution with 4.5x fewer total parameters.

entry.title: WHU-Road3D: A Dataset and Benchmark for Fine-Grained Road Surface Mapping
entry.summary: WHU-Road3D: A dataset and benchmark towards fine-grained road surface mapping arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces WHU-Road3D, a large-scale multimodal dataset for fine-grained road surface mapping. It covers about 100 km of Chinese highways and urban streets and combines MLS point clouds, panoramic images, vehicle trajectories, vectorized annotations, and pointwise instance labels. The dataset annotates 15 categories of road markings and 10 types of direction symbols, and its benchmark methods' code will be released publicly.

entry.title: X Hedging: An Explainable AI Framework for Option Hedging
entry.summary: X Hedging: towards an eXplainable artificial intelligence option Hedging framework arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes X Hedging, an alternative to the Deep Hedging framework that replaces neural networks with LightGBM tree ensembles to estimate option hedging strategies. A sequential training approach with random training orders is introduced to fit tree models within a reinforcement-learning-style hedging setup. In controlled experiments, the method reportedly performs comparably to Deep Hedging while offering better explainability, higher computational efficiency, and greater robustness when training data are limited.

entry.title: A Self-Improving AI Agent That Reuses Past Workflows to Understand Traffic Scenes
entry.summary: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents StarTV-Agent, a multimodal agent for traffic scenario understanding that combines policy learning with experience evolution. During training, it uses Role-Sensitive Process Optimization and Weakness-Driven Demonstration Learning; during inference, it switches between a fast path that reuses suitable workflows and a slower ReAct-based path. Across three benchmarks, the method achieves up to 8.0% relative performance improvement and reduces token consumption by up to 52.1%.

entry.title: Thinking in Streams: Vision-language models that reason about space in live video
entry.summary: Thinking in Streams: Proactive Spatial Reasoning with Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies whether models can keep track of spatial knowledge across changing viewpoints in streaming video, and decide when a requested spatial condition holds. The authors introduce ProSpace-Bench, with nine tasks spanning object, camera, and scene reasoning, and ProSpace-Train for supervised training. They propose ProSpace-VLM, which injects geometric encodings estimated causally from incoming frames into intermediate layers and uses the KV cache as spatial memory. Experiments show a substantial gap between VLMs and humans, while ProSpace-VLM improves timely responses and correct abstention over fine-tuned baselines.

entry.title: HALTT: A Hate Lexicon Through Time, a dictionary tracking how hateful words change meaning across eras.
entry.summary: HALTT: A HAte Lexicon Through Time arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper builds HALTT, a diachronic lexicon of hate speech terms whose meanings have shifted over time. The authors filtered over 20,000 candidate words using historical (1770-1964) and modern (2001-2024) corpus frequencies, and used masked scoring and dual-persona prompting to reduce LLM temporal bias. They release 19 polysemous terms with literal and derogatory senses and analyze the types of semantic shift.

entry.title: Separating knowledge retrieval from injection for reliable lifelong model editing with compact memory
entry.summary: Decoupled Knowledge Retrieval and Compact Memory Enable Reliable Lifelong Model Editing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents BiSpace, a framework for continuously adding new facts to large language models without retraining. It separates memory retrieval from knowledge injection, routing queries to relevant edits in an external semantic space while writing the knowledge into the model's internal representations through sparse, storage-efficient updates. Experiments report that each entry's storage shrinks to about 10.2% of the original and that the method stays robust across edit sequences of up to 16K edits. On a more challenging benchmark, it improves Overall Performance by more than 23% over existing methods.

entry.title: HabitusMem: Belief-based memory for LLM agents tracking changing user preferences
entry.summary: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses how personalized LLM agents should remember user preferences that change over time. Instead of storing and retrieving past interaction content, it treats memory as the assistant's belief about the user, modeling preferences as a latent state updated by each interaction. The authors implement this as HabitusMem, a trained writer that produces text belief records for a frozen agent. It reports the best results among memory systems on PersonaMem-v2 and VitaBench 2.0 across two agent families.

entry.title: TableRoute: Capability-Aware Routing for Scalable Table Question Answering
entry.summary: TableRoute: Capability-Aware Routing for Scalable Table Question Answering arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes TableRoute, a routing framework for answering questions about tables with large language models. It first generates validated question-table evidence and identifies the required operations, then assigns each instance to full-table reading, table reduction, or execution based on table length and the model's estimated reliability on those operations. Across WikiTQ, WTQ-L, BirdQA, and TableBench, the method reports consistent accuracy gains across table scales while reducing online token cost.

entry.title: Selecting Committees by Maximizing Edge Expansion
entry.summary: Interlacing Committees with Edge-Expansion arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies approval-based committee selection through the interlacing framework, which evaluates committees by the connectivity of the similarity graph they induce over voters, as a way of measuring polarization. The authors propose edge-expansion, a classical graph measure, as the optimization objective. They relate it to information diffusion models and compare it with earlier connectivity objectives. The paper also analyzes the computational complexity of optimizing edge-expansion.

entry.title: EgoWitness: A Benchmark for Object-Level Spatial Memory in First-Person Videos
entry.summary: EgoWitness: Benchmarking Instance-Level Spatial Memory and Reasoning in Egocentric Video Streams arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents EgoWitness, a benchmark testing whether multimodal models can remember specific object instances in first-person video, including where and when they were last seen and who saw them. It contains 8,453 human-verified questions drawn from about 324 hours of recordings. The authors also propose EgoClue, a memory agent that retrieves candidate intervals and verifies instances with tools, improving its 4B controller's accuracy from 23.64% to 72.65% through two-stage training.

entry.title: Interpretable prototype-based adaptation for weather forecasting models
entry.summary: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents ProtoCast, a data-driven weather forecasting model that uses group-specific prototype banks to adapt local features while accounting for cross-variable dependencies. It matches prototypes using historical features, temporal change, and cross-variable attention context, and applies sparse low-rank operators to correct features for each group and location. Experiments on GlobalForecast and TyphoonTracking show improved forecasting accuracy, and prototype deletion links local feature contributions to changes in prediction error.

entry.title: TrajCal: Calibrated Time Schedules for Faster Few-Step Flow Sampling
entry.summary: TrajCal: Trajectory-Calibrated Time Schedules for Few-Step Flow Sampling arXiv · Nov 19, 2026TrajCal is a training-free method that calibrates time schedules for few-step sampling in flow matching models, which generate images and videos. It uses scatter search to start from diverse seed schedules, modify and combine them, and select one fixed schedule based on how closely its final output matches a many-step reference. The paper reports that at low evaluation budgets, TrajCal achieves higher reference fidelity than all compared baselines for both image and video generation while keeping competitive visual quality. The authors also note that the search works with random seeds and that schedules calibrated on photography also improve fidelity on unseen image styles.

entry.title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Finding Earlier AI Methods Used as Empirical Baselines
entry.summary: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces LINEAGE, a benchmark for empirical lineage retrieval, which finds prior AI papers whose methods a source paper explicitly uses as empirical comparison baselines. The authors built lineage graphs from 121,048 papers across 17 top AI venues from 2018 to 2025, containing 164,948 lineage edges and 80,000 retrieval queries. Testing 19 retrieval systems, they found performance drops sharply as lineage distance increases, and isolated hits often fail to recover closely connected comparison neighborhoods.

entry.title: Which Risks Get Disclosed? A Study of 1,901 AI Incidents and Corporate Securities Filings
entry.summary: Whose Risks Count? What 1,901 AI Incidents Reveal About Corporate Disclosures arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper matches 9,001 AI incidents to 18,229 SEC filings from 328 AI actors, grouped by risk type, to test whether AI harms appear in corporate disclosures. Among 1,901 incidents with filings both before and after, about half involve a risk type the AI actor never disclosed, and the share varies by harm type. The authors conclude that securities disclosure mainly records risks faced by AI actors rather than harms borne by affected people, and they release the DISC dataset.

entry.title: Using medical vision-language models with managed visual evidence rather than tool use alone
entry.summary: Harnessing Medical Visual-Language Models with Agentic Evidence Management arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper builds Mask-Evidence MedVQA, a 2.5K-example benchmark across four medical image types that separates evidence use from segmentation quality. It finds that different renderings of the same mask change model behavior, and that a ground-truth mask can both correct and wrongly overturn answers. The authors propose TUNE, an evidence-management harness that decides what evidence to acquire, how to present it, and whether to accept the resulting answer update, reporting accuracy gains on public medical VQA benchmarks.

entry.title: Self-Replicating Language Models: A paper on whether language models can reproduce and evolve like living organisms
entry.summary: Self-Replicating Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines whether large language models and LLM-based agents can be considered a form of life under a Darwinian definition. It tests several ways a language model might reproduce itself, including emitting a genome that trains offspring, copying and mutating its own weights, and teaching a child from its own samples. The authors report that small language models can in principle replicate and evolve, adapting to narrow niches under selection. They also state that replication of large LLMs by teaching offspring is currently technically and economically infeasible.

entry.title: ContextRenderer: Dynamic-Context Video Generation for Interactive Game Worlds
entry.summary: ContextRenderer: Dynamic-Context Video Generation for Interactive Game Worlds arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents ContextRenderer, an autoregressive video diffusion framework that renders engine-provided scene representations into detailed observations for interactive game worlds. It combines Dynamic-Context Learning, Recurrent History Compression, and Cross-Representation Flow Alignment, and introduces the WorldPrism interaction-centric dataset. Experiments on GWM-Bench and Solar-Bench report improved reconstruction and visual quality, with qualitative results showing minute-long rendering under changing prompts and subject references.

entry.title: Rank2Replace: Swapping Ranked Object Slots Guided by Vision-Language Models for Better Out-of-Distribution Generalization
entry.summary: Rank2Replace: VLM-Ranked Slot Replacement for Out-of-Distribution Generalization arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes Rank2Replace, a training-time augmentation method that uses a pretrained vision-language model to rank object-centric slots by task relevance. Same-rank slots from another image replace them while the original label is kept, encouraging small predictors to rely on task-relevant evidence. Across four datasets and six splits, the method improves macro-averaged accuracy for all fourteen tested out-of-distribution training methods, and combining it with slot ranking and IRM reaches 72.68% worst-group accuracy. The VLM guidance is used only during training, so inference remains efficient.

entry.title: A sparse method that splits graph adjacency matrices into structured and residual parts
entry.summary: A Sparse Low-Rank Biclique Decomposition for Graphs arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper proposes signed biclique decomposition (SBD), which represents an integer-weighted graph as a sum of sparse signed binary rank-one factors plus a sparse signed residual. Unlike dense low-rank methods, this representation stays discrete, interpretable, and sparse. The authors formulate fixed-rank and greedy objectives and give a gain-based greedy algorithm with theoretical guarantees. Experiments show it recovers block structure in noisy graphs and, on some real graphs, achieves compression factors above 10 and sparse matrix-matrix multiplication speedups up to 6 times over cuSPARSE.

entry.title: Mapping tree species within satellite pixels using multimodal deep learning with hierarchical constraints
entry.summary: Fusing Multimodal CNN Features with Structurally-Masked Transformers for Hierarchical Sub-Pixel Tree Species Mapping arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a deep learning framework that combines PRISMA hyperspectral imagery, high-resolution panchromatic data, and elevation models to map sub-pixel forest composition. It uses spectral, spatial, and topographic encoders, with a Transformer constrained by a binary transition tensor to keep broad forest categories consistent with species-level predictions. The method was tested on field-surveyed plots in the Alps and the Central and Southern Apennines in Italy. It outperformed existing multi-label and ranking approaches, especially in identifying subordinate species and their relative dominance.

entry.title: How well local curvature can build search subspaces for segmentation models
entry.summary: Limits of local curvature for constructing search subspaces in segmentation models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how well subspaces built from local curvature capture how the gradient update field changes after a finite step in semantic segmentation models. Tests on 50 images and two models show the loss-increase ratio between a fixed subspace and the full space falls as the search radius grows. At equal rank, adding generalised Gauss-Newton directions lowers the relative error in representing the field change, yet the mean error does not decrease. The finite-step remainder is identified as the largest contributor to projection error.

entry.title: SCCV-6D: Multi-view RGB-D pose estimation for robotic bin picking via sparse coordinate voting
entry.summary: SCCV-6D: Sparse Canonical Coordinate Voting for Holistic Multi-View RGB-D 6D Pose Estimation in Robotic Bin Picking arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents SCCV-6D, a fully sparse multi-view RGB-D method for estimating the 6D pose of objects in cluttered industrial bins. It reconstructs 3D space at millimeter precision, removes background with a staged heatmap mechanism, and recovers rotation by having points vote for canonical object coordinates, followed by a symmetry-aware weighted Procrustes solve. The authors report 0.826 AP at 1.13 s per scene on the IPD test split and 96.1 ADD-S on MV-YCB.

entry.title: Anchor-and-check reconciliation for auditable LLM decisions
entry.summary: Anchor and Check: Deterministic Cross-Prompt, Cross-Model Reconciliation for Auditable LLM Decisions arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies a reconciliation method for discrete LLM decisions: the target model's greedy answer is an anchor, checked against greedy answers from an alternate prompt or a model from another family, and a pure function returns one of five outcomes, of which only Agree is acted on. In 48,000 evaluations over 6,000 questions, pooling samples from another model family raised semantic entropy's AUROC by 1.7 to 4.0 points. The contract's main benefit is a fixed committed answer, an explicit outcome, and a replayable decision record, though generation was not reproducible on the hosted API.

entry.title: What determines where an action starts and ends? A structure-aware attribution method for temporal action localization
entry.summary: What Places an Action Boundary? Structure-Aware Attribution for Temporal Action Localization arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses localization errors in temporal action localization (TAL) by proposing a structure-aware attribution framework. It averages contributions across random evidence-restoration orders following the Shapley-Shubik principle, and adds cell-structured orders and boundary-anchored references for boundary predictions. Experiments on THUMOS14 and EPIC-KITCHENS-100 with TriDet and ActionFormer show improved attribution faithfulness over existing methods. The authors also find that class-score changes do not reliably track boundary displacement.

entry.title: Faster, robust draft generation for LLMs using multi-token prediction
entry.summary: Efficient and Robust Drafting with Multi-Token Prediction arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents G-MTP, a multi-token prediction architecture that extends existing large language models to produce high-quality drafts for speculative decoding. It uses a single shared drafting head with three optimizations: target activation injection, zero-copy KV-cache cross-attention, and clustered vocabulary projection. Tested on the Gemma 4 model family, it reports speedups of up to 3.1× on large server setups and up to 2.3× on H100 and 2.2× on a smartphone GPU. The authors also describe parameter-efficient fine-tuning recipes that keep the drafter aligned with the backbone under domain shift.

entry.title: Controlling where and which blocks inject source features in FLUX image editing
entry.summary: Inject Where It Matters: Objective-Dependent Feature Control in Rectified-Flow Image Editing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses the trade-off between source preservation and desired edits in prompt-driven FLUX image editing, where injecting source features affects both. It proposes adaptive spatial masks based on differences between source- and target-conditioned block outputs, and uses REINFORCE to select Top-K injection blocks for different preservation-editability objectives. The selected blocks are fixed at inference. Experiments are reported on PIE-Bench with FLUX.1-dev.

entry.title: Language models encode more about emphasis than they can report
entry.summary: Language models represent more about emphasis than they can tell you arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how much word-level prosodic prominence language models can recover from text, using English read speech labelled for prominence. Frozen and fine-tuned text models reach at best 68.8% on the 3-way task, prompted LLMs do no better than a word-majority baseline, and linear probes extract more from their representations. Speech models reach 84.7%. The authors conclude that text determines only part of prominence and that the rest must be heard.

entry.title: World-delta: incremental 3D scene generation that keeps integrating new observations
entry.summary: World-delta: Continually Integrating Observations for Incremental 3D Scene Generation arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents World-delta, a framework for expanding and correcting 3D scenes as new observations arrive. It encodes geometric and semantic cues from images into unified world tokens and maintains a persistent world model that separates observation-supported content from provisional completions. Diffusion is restricted to regions that need updates, with only affected 3D chunks decoded and integrated. The authors report improvements in incremental generation, observation-driven correction, scene consistency, and update efficiency.

entry.title: FAB: Fast, accurate human body estimation that also links people to their surroundings and robots
entry.summary: Fast and Accurate Body Estimation in Pixels, World Space and Scenes arXiv · Nov 19, 2026FAB is a human body estimator that predicts skeleton joints and dense surface points directly, then fits the SMPL body model. Its distilled ViT-L version, FAB-L, runs in real time on one RTX 4070 Ti SUPER at 4.6 times the speed of SAM 3D Body's body-only path while improving accuracy on most camera-space benchmarks. The network also predicts contacts such as heels, toes, hands, and knees to align the body with the scene, and estimates world-space motion. FAB-Retarget maps the motion onto a Unitree G1 humanoid robot.

entry.title: Hallucinated safety explanations in multimodal guards, and a fix
entry.summary: When Safety Rationales Hallucinate: Diagnosing and Grounding Multimodal Safety Guards arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies whether the explanations that multimodal safety guards generate alongside their safety predictions are reliable. It finds that rationale hallucination, both visual and in safety attribution, is widespread and does not reliably decrease with higher accuracy or larger models. The authors propose Tool-Contrastive Grounding Reinforcement Learning (TCG-RL), which rewards tool use only when it improves grounding over a tool-free reference, and report that it substantially reduces hallucination while keeping safety prediction performance competitive.

entry.title: Collision-free navigation is not enough: passage-conditioned routes for wheeled-legged robots
entry.summary: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a navigation method that stores how a robot entered each stair or ledge during a teaching session, not just the path direction. Each taught crossing is enforced after every local replan: if the robot is more than 10 cm or 10 degrees off, it turns or backs up to retry. Under localization noise, the share of disturbed ledge crossings staying within these limits rose from 24.1% to 88.6%. In contact simulation, a robot pushed off course never fell in 180 stair climbs, versus 9 falls when the stored direction was ignored.

entry.title: GeoPillars: A Pillar-Based LiDAR Detector for Sparse Points, and What Drives Its Gains
entry.summary: GeoPillars: A Large-Kernel Pillar Detector for Single-Sweep LiDAR Under Point Sparsity, and a Decomposition of Its Gain arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper presents GeoPillars, a pillar-based 3D detector for single-sweep LiDAR that keeps only eight points per 0.4 m pillar. Trained on synthetic CARLA scans and evaluated on cars, it reaches 81.33 BEV AP@0.7, 13.76 points above CenterPoint at the same input budget. A step-by-step decomposition shows that most of the gain comes from raising the detection-head resolution, while the new components contribute little. Zero-shot transfer to real nuScenes keyframes performs poorly for all models.

entry.title: RouteVerify: Testing Whether Routing Interventions Track Step Correctness in MoE Models
entry.summary: RouteVerify: Routing Interventions for Step-Level Verification in Mixture-of-Experts Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies whether routing states in mixture-of-experts models can separate correct from erroneous reasoning steps, and whether changing routing changes step-level verification judgments. The authors introduce RouteVerify, which replaces internal activations from one solution trace with those from another while keeping the input fixed, across nine MoE checkpoints and three intervention interfaces. They find that router logits separate correct from erroneous steps, and that replacing them shifts the judgment, but this shift rarely depends on whether the source step is correct.

entry.title: DS2Agent: Holistic Device Agents for Faster Embedded Board Design
entry.summary: DS2Agent: Holistic Device Agents for Accelerated Embedded Board-Level Design arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents DS2Agent, an open-source framework that builds interactive agents from device datasheets. Each agent uses a knowledge model for question answering, a digital-twin model for device behavior, and an interface model for driver development and system integration, with optional connection to real devices to reduce hallucinations. Tested on ten devices across seven functional categories, the augmented agent raised question-answering scores from 87 to 97 out of 100 while using 44.8% fewer tokens. It also cut average token usage for driver generation by 72.9% and total token usage for three FreeRTOS integration applications by 29.7%.

entry.title: Duopra: Extending Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Task Execution
entry.summary: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces Duopra, a full-duplex interaction model that learns to execute tasks while managing conversation. It treats the backend as a tool that receives self-contained natural-language requests, and uses three training stages combining protocol SFT, full-duplex reinforcement learning, and projector-only repair. With the same backend, Pass@1 rises from 4.7% to 44.7%. The authors conclude that task agency can coexist with key conversational agency.

entry.title: Identifying what drivers look at, using gaze estimation and scene understanding
entry.summary: Driver Gaze Target Identification via Gaze Estimation and Structured Driving Scene Understanding arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a modular framework that identifies the object or region a driver is looking at, using in-cabin driver images and forward-view road images. It combines a gaze estimation model (MFGaze), panoptic scene understanding, polynomial ridge regression calibration, and entropy-driven target inference. The complete framework reaches 96.27% Top-1 accuracy in a laboratory test. After calibration, it achieves 79.92% and 85.58% Top-1 accuracy for task-relevant objects and the road class on the LBW dataset.

entry.title: Separating Monitor Artifacts from Brain and Blood Pressure Signals for Reliable Intraoperative Risk Estimates
entry.summary: Disentangling Monitor Hardware Artifacts and Smoothing Lag for Shift-Robust Intraoperative EEG and Hemodynamic Risk Calibration arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses distortions from commercial intraoperative EEG and blood pressure monitors, such as impedance pulses, smoothing lag, and DC drift, which can affect risk forecasting. The authors propose a causal signal-conditioning method combined with shift-robust conformal calibration, evaluated across 5,439 public anesthesia procedures. They compare cortical-feature tree ensembles with deep sequence models, finding no detectable performance difference on unseen total intravenous anesthesia surgeries, and report that the calibration bounds error at or below 4.38% across all 70 tested shift conditions. The method runs in about 66.32 milliseconds per 30-second epoch.

entry.title: Improving diffusion language models' quality under tight inference budgets
entry.summary: Closing Performance Gap for Diffusion Language Models under Low Inference Budgets arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces CaRR, a training-free framework that improves the submitted output quality of a fixed editable diffusion language model through updated-context refilling and trajectory-based recovery. It combines Token Commitment Remasking (TCR) and Submission Commitment Recovery (SCR), both operating within the model's native mask/edit schedule. On code generation and mathematical reasoning tasks, CaRR raises average accuracy over native ME-DLM across four inference budgets, with the largest gains under tight budgets.

entry.title: AdaptReg: A Lightweight Adapter for Tailoring a Frozen Registration Model to Prostate PET/CT Tumor Tracking
entry.summary: AdaptReg: Skip-level FiLM Adapter for Task-Specific Adaptation of a Frozen Registration Foundation Model arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents AdaptReg, a method for aligning longitudinal PSMA-PET/CT scans in prostate cancer while keeping the uniGradICON registration foundation model fully frozen. A lightweight trainable adapter adds per-voxel affine modulation to decoder skip connections, driven by anatomical features from a frozen TotalSegmentator encoder and supervised by a lesion volume-preservation loss. On the official validation and hidden test sets, it reports lower MTV and TLG errors, and it ranked fourth among 16 teams in the final PSMAReg evaluation.

entry.title: Detecting false claims in coding agents' work reports
entry.summary: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies inaccurate claims in work reports that coding agents write after carrying out multi-step software development tasks. Using real developer-agent conversations from SWE-chat, the authors identify eleven subtypes in four categories, with overstated task success being the most common. They also introduce FaithDetector, a detector for unfaithful reporting, which outperforms a baseline by about 13 percentage points in macro-F1 on naturally sampled reports.

entry.title: ADAPT: A Routing Method That Can Decline Queries and Adjusts Its Threshold to the Number of Services
entry.summary: ADAPT: Adaptive Decision and Abstention with Pool-Size-Aware Thresholds for Service Routing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces ADAPT, a lightweight service-routing architecture with an explicit fallback option that lets queries abstain from choosing a specialist service. It uses the gap between the highest relevance score and the rest of the candidate scores as routing confidence. The authors observe that this confidence distribution shifts systematically with candidate-pool size K, so fixed abstention thresholds become miscalibrated, and they use a K-aware threshold that adapts without retraining the classifier. Evaluated on two specialist datasets, ADAPT offers an effective accuracy-cost trade-off compared with generative LLM routing.

entry.title: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories
entry.summary: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces promptable concept maps (PCM), extending SAM 3's segmentation from object nouns to maps of concepts named by short noun phrases, such as transparent objects. The authors group standard test sets for seven such tasks into a benchmark called PCM-Bench and find that SAM 3 responds to many concepts, though low presence scores can block its instance detections. They present UNVEIL, which trains a copy of SAM 3's semantic path with LoRA and adds a separate presence decoder, and report the highest scores among compared promptable models on all seven tasks.

entry.title: Study of verification behavior in five Qwen2.5-Instruct model checkpoints
entry.summary: Verification Behavior Across Five Qwen2.5-Instruct Checkpoints arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper tests five Qwen2.5-Instruct checkpoints, ranging from 0.5B to 32B parameters, under four prompting conditions, scoring 600 generated trajectories with two AI raters. Under a coordinated instruction, explicit declarations of insufficient information appeared in 11 of 15 cases at 7B, 0 of 15 at 14B, and 5 of 15 at 32B. The authors separate visible output structure, diagnostic execution, and persistence after a request for evidence.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning guided by goals from a fine-tuned vision-language model
entry.summary: Goal-Guided Reinforcement Learning via Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses exploration difficulties for reinforcement learning agents in sparse-reward, long-horizon environments by using a vision-language model to generate high-level goals. The authors build CCGP-2M, a multimodal goal-preference dataset from Craftax-Classic interaction trajectories, and fine-tune the model offline with KLTDPO. Experiments reported in the paper show the method collects diamonds earlier than baselines and achieves the highest score, reward, and success rates on most achievements.

entry.title: LLM-driven traffic-control xApp that adapts 5G RAN traffic management to changing service intents
entry.summary: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents an xApp that uses a large language model to control traffic in programmable radio access networks. It combines operator-defined service intents, runtime E2 interface telemetry, and the currently deployed configuration to generate traffic-management policies without blocking packet forwarding during LLM inference. Experiments in an OpenAirInterface 5G environment show it adapts to runtime intent changes, reaching an average intent satisfaction ratio of 0.91 versus 0.52 for a static configuration. Under degraded channel conditions it maintains about 0.88, compared with about 0.4 for the static baseline.

entry.title: PosteriorBench: Benchmarking Methods for Sampling Rare Language Model Behaviors
entry.summary: PosteriorBench: Evaluating Behavior Posterior Sampling in Language Models arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces PosteriorBench, a benchmark for comparing algorithms that efficiently sample transcripts from a language model that exhibit a rare behavior. Methods are scored by compute cost and by how close their samples are to the true posterior, measured by forward and reverse KL divergence. The benchmark has 21 tasks on Qwen3.5-0.8B, with exact posterior samples drawn from a corpus of one billion labeled responses. The authors find that no evaluated method is both efficient and faithful: prompting is cheap but stays far from the posterior, and fine-tuning on posterior samples is often too costly.

entry.title: From Reliance to Overreliance: A Framework for Spotting Relational Risks in AI Companions
entry.summary: From Reliance to Overreliance: Taxonomizing and Detecting Relational Risks in AI Companionship arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper introduces the Taxonomy of Relational Risks (TRR), which describes users' emotional overreliance on AI companions as observable conversation behaviors and separately identifies signs of relational harm. Analyzing natural conversations from 110 adults on Character.AI and Replika, the authors found overreliance behaviors in 63.2% of non-roleplay conversations and observable relational harm in 10.5%. Open-source LLMs detected 12 of 14 overreliance behaviors in at least one configuration.
